title: Senior Software Integration Engineer
description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title and Summary

Senior Software Integration Engineer

Overview

The SME team is looking for a Senior Software Integration Engineer who can contribute independently in complex situations while supporting quality, engineering, and delivery goals. This role requires strong experience in agile work management, integration testing, quality assurance, requirements management, SDLC practices, systems integration, troubleshooting, web services, workflow management, and test automation.
The ideal candidate will plan, prioritize, and manage work using agile practices to enable iterative delivery, collaboration, adaptability, and continuous improvement. They will partner with developers and engineering teams to review source code, identify issues, improve quality, and promote maintainability and coding standards.
This position is responsible for designing, executing, and maintaining tests that validate interactions across integrated components, systems, services, APIs, data flows, interfaces, and dependencies. The candidate will help establish and maintain QA processes and standards that prevent defects, optimize performance, improve customer satisfaction, and support compliance.
The role also requires strong understanding of requirements management, SDLC, systems integration, web services, troubleshooting, and workflow management. The candidate should be a key contributor who can guide others informally and help teams deliver reliable, maintainable solutions.
Role

In this role, you will:
• Perform QE activities across assigned projects, including test planning, strategy, validation, automation, and release readiness.
• Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to enhance testing processes and strengthen quality practices.
• Contribute to SME QE teams focused on test validation and automation within assigned projects.
• Design, execute, and maintain integration tests to validate interactions between systems, services, APIs, data flows, interfaces, and dependencies.
• Establish and maintain QA processes and standards that prevent defects, improve quality, optimize performance, and support customer expectations.
• Apply agile work management practices to plan, prioritize, and manage work effectively in iterative delivery environments.
• Partner with product owners, developers, and delivery teams to review requirements, clarify acceptance criteria, manage changes, identify risks, and ensure testability throughout the SDLC.
• Support SDLC activities including requirements, design, coding, testing, deployment, and maintenance to ensure solutions remain high quality and maintainable.
• Contribute to systems integration by validating communication, interoperability, and reliability across diverse technologies, processes, applications, and services.
• Implement and support UI, API, backend, and integration automation using tools such as Playwright, Cypress, and API automation frameworks.
• Support API performance testing and performance validation using tools such as Gatling and BlazeMeter.
• Troubleshoot complex issues across systems, applications, services, integrations, test environments, and networks using structured methods and tools.
• Evaluate source code written by developers to identify and address potential issues, support maintainability, improve quality, and ensure adherence to coding standards and best practices.
• Analyze workflows, identify bottlenecks, streamline procedures, monitor progress, allocate resources, and adapt processes to ensure work moves smoothly from one stage to the next.
• Contribute to CI/CD and DevOps practices by supporting automated test execution, version control, and integration of test automation into delivery pipelines.
• Provide technical guidance to team members, support proof-of-concepts, coach others informally, and help teams adopt scalable and maintainable test automation practices.
• Communicate status, risks, dependencies, and quality insights clearly to stakeholders and leadership.
• Promote agile ways of working, continuous learning, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement across the team.

All About You / Experience

The ideal candidate for this position should have:
• Strong experience in quality engineering, test strategy, planning, automation, QA, and software validation across complex technology programs.
• Ability to apply skills independently and consistently in complex or nuanced situations while supporting broader business, delivery, and quality goals.
• Strong knowledge of agile principles and practices, including planning, prioritization, iterative delivery, collaboration, adaptability, and continuous improvement.
• Experience collaborating with developers and engineering teams to review source code, identify potential issues, improve maintainability, and promote coding standards and best practices.
• Hands-on experience with UI and API automation tools such as Playwright and Cypress.
• Strong experience in API integration testing and backend validation.
• Experience designing and maintaining integration tests that validate data flows, interfaces, dependencies, web services, and system interactions.
• Experience with API performance testing and exposure to performance testing tools such as Gatling and BlazeMeter.
• Strong understanding of requirements management, including documenting, analyzing, tracing, prioritizing, agreeing on, and communicating requirements and changes to stakeholders.
• Strong understanding of software development life cycle practices, including requirements gathering, design, coding, testing, deployment, and maintenance.
• Experience with systems integration, including validating communication and interoperability across applications, services, technologies, and processes.
• Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills, with the ability to systematically identify, diagnose, and resolve technical issues across systems, applications, services, test environments, and networks.
• Experience with web services and standardized protocols that enable communication, data exchange, interoperability, scalability, and integration across diverse systems.
• Ability to analyze workflows, identify bottlenecks, streamline procedures, monitor progress, allocate resources, and adapt processes to achieve outcomes.
• Working knowledge of version control tools such as Git.
• Experience with API testing tools such as Insomnia.
• Experience with test case management tools such as XRay.
• Experience with project management tools such as Jira.
• Exposure to cloud platforms, preferably Azure.
• Familiarity with AI-assisted engineering and quality practices, including GitHub Copilot, Playwright MCP servers, and automation accelerators.
• Ability to work on proof-of-concepts.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and present quality insights clearly.
• Self-driven, proactive, adaptable, and committed to continuous improvement.

Corporate Security Responsibility


All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:

  • Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

  • Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

  • Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

  • Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

title: Commercial Underwriting and Portfolio Risk
description:
Job Description:

The Commercial Underwriting and Portfolio Risk role is responsible for the timely and accurate underwriting of new and existing commercial credit lines through business financial statement analysis, investigations and communications with all relevant stakeholders. This role's primary objective is to conduct detailed financial statement analysis for both public and privately held businesses, continuously manage credit exposures, and perform customer due diligence for new and existing clients to ensure that the Wheels US credit portfolio is of strong credit quality and within the established risk appetite.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES – ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Underwrite new and existing credit facilities through financial analysis, due diligence, and review of deal terms, structure, and legal documentation
  • Conduct due diligence on prospects and clients with senior management
  • Construct and manage DCF (discounted cash flow) and cash flow models including sensitivity analyses to mitigate risk across diverse portfolios
  • Present comprehensive credit packages including detailed free cash flow analysis, capital structure assessment, and projected asset risk coverage to executive leadership
  • Build scalable and efficient credit analysis and monitoring processes
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to assess projected asset risk coverage, department initiatives, system development, and workflow improvements
  • Ensure accurate internal risk ratings and support portfolio management,
  • Conduct training to assist with the development of less experienced team members
  • Perform ad hoc company, industry, and portfolio analysis
  • Other duties as assigned

LEADERSHIP RESPONSIBLITIES

  • This position’s leadership responsibilities involve demonstrating ethics and integrity, developing adaptability, displaying drive and purpose, and exhibiting leadership stature to members to key stakeholders for the origination and presentation of credit requests

COMPETENCIES - SKILLS

  • Leveraged loan or private credit analysis experience including extensive financial statement analysis abilities and understanding of industry trends
  • Knowledge of credit risk scoring methodologies and credit risk mitigation techniques
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Excel and ability to integrate AI tools into the research and credit analysis process
  • Ability to use visualization software (Tableau or Power BI) to create dashboards, preferred
  • Strong time and project management skills to successfully work on multiple analytical assignments without loss in quality while meeting credit renewal timelines

​EDUCATION and EXPERIENCE

  • Minimum 5 years of commercial credit underwriting/analysis experience, preferably at a financial institution
  • Bachelor's degree in business or finance field, in conjunction with formal credit training
  • Effective communicator at all levels of the organization
  • Experience with financial modeling in Excel (Pivot tables, Lookups, Formulas)
  • Experience creating dashboards using Tableau or PowerBI, preferred


CORE VALUES

At Wheels, we believe in fostering a culture that is built on our Core Values and Guiding Principles. We cultivate a culture of excellence and innovation by upholding these values, driving our collective success and growth.

  • Integrity – Always act with integrity and honesty.
  • One Team – Treat others with dignity and respect; act as a cohesive, inclusive and accountable team that is making a difference.
  • Innovation – Drive continuous improvement, spark creativity and embrace next generation thinking.
  • Customer Success – Ensure that customer and driver success is at the heart of everything we do.

CULTURAL ATTRIBUTES

At Wheels, our culture guides us how we work every day, and we look for team members who show these behaviors:

  • Discipline Drives Quality – Plan the Trip: Think proactively, hold a high bar, follow through by leveraging experience and systems. To produce quality outcomes, we must be intentional and deliberate in everything we do, from big bets to daily execution.
  • Intellectually Curious – Fuel Your Minds: Be bold, challenge assumptions, think differently, look outside the box. Strive to unlock your own thinking and create new possibilities.
  • Commit and Deliver – Own It: Take responsibility for your work, from start to finish, and be accountable for the results. Think and act like an owner of the business.
  • Relationships Matter – Share the Ride: Trust is central, both with key internal and external stakeholders. Relationships are not a side effect of work but a driver of success.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS, PHYSICAL DEMANDS and WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Work Environment: This position can sit in either Alpharetta, GA or Schaumburg, Ill and operates in a professional office environment.
  • Position Type/Standard Schedule: This is a full-time, hybrid position (Tue-Thu onsite) Monday through Friday 8a-5pm.
  • Travel: Minimal travel of 5% is expected for this position. (Very rare).
  • Physical Demands: Speak, hear, and see, and use hand and fingers for computer keyboard and phone. Sit or stand for extended periods of time. Reach above head to pull paper attachments.

title: QC Inspector 1
description:
The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.


Meet the team:
A receiving inspection QC inspector assists in maintaining high-quality standards by supporting quality control processes, conducting inspections, and managing documentation, contributing to the overall quality and compliance of products or services within an organization.


Where you come in:
As a member of the Receiving Inspection team, the inspector is responsible to ensure the activities related to the inspection functions in a manner which meets company standards and methods as determined by quality assurance or other engineering departments.


What makes you successful:
• You will perform inspections, check testing and sampling procedures for incoming components, materials, subassemblies, and product as conforming to specified requirements in accordance with material specification, drawing and quality assurance standards.
• You will prepare, record, and update receiving inspection report form.
• You will ensure all paperwork contains accurate and legible information. Any discrepancies are noted on the receiving inspection report form.
• You will ensure all documentation is legible, complete, and correct per current Good Manufacturing Practices.
• You will perform transaction related to QA sample or nonconforming materials in a defined system if applicable.
• You will apply approval label, release, and move inspection lots to approve locations, or vice versa apply rejection label and quarantine the nonconforming inspection lots once analytical data is evaluated.
• You will initiate and assist with the NCMR process during incoming inspection.
• You will monitor equipment and instrumentation to ensure it is clean and safe to use.
• You will use the Microsoft Suite of products: Word, Excel, Outlooks.
• You will adhere to all GMP, safety guidelines and company standards always.
• You will assume and perform other duties as assigned.

Experience and Education Requirements:
• Typically requires a high school certificate (SPM), candidates with less than 2 years of relevant industry experience and/or training are welcome to apply. Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply.
• Good interpersonal and teamwork skills.
• Must be able to flex schedule to work in different shifts to meet demand.
• Receiving inspection and/or QA/QC experience.
• 0-2 years in the medical device industry or manufacturing industry previous experience.
• Ability to understand drawings and tolerances.

title: Clinical Lab Scientist - Laboratory - Full Time 8 Hours Days (6:00AM to 2:30PM)) (Non-Union, Non-Exempt)
description:
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS AND CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Able to analyze and priorities work duties.

  • Able to identify and solve technical problems and difficulties during routine testing.

  • Adhere to the laboratory's quality control policies, document all quality control activities, instrument and procedural calibrations and maintenance performed, approval of appropriate technical coordinator.

  • Assists in developing a recording system to ensure that necessary controls in the work steps are documented.

  • Assists in developing and installing quality control standards to assure accuracy in test results.

  • Assists in training and orienting new employees and students.

  • Assists the section supervisor in reviewing and solving quality control problems.

  • Assumes the role of a section supervisor when required.

  • Be capable of identifying problems that may adversely affect test performance or reporting of test results and either must correct the problems or immediately notify the general supervisor, technical supervisor, clinical consultant or director; and

  • Contributes to a safe, organized and efficient workplace by complying with established hospital and departmental policies.

  • Demonstrates knowledge of theory behind the tests being performed. Requires a degree of skill commensurate with the individual's education, training or experience, and technical abilities.

  • Document all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from the laboratory's established performance specifications.

  • Each individual performing high complexity testing.

  • Each individual performs only those high complexity tests that are authorized by the laboratory.

  • Ensures professional development by assuming responsibility and accountability for current competency, licensure and credentialing files.

  • Ensures that Staff Clinical Laboratory Technicians and other trainees are prepared for their responsibilities by providing objectives, instruction and guidance as appropriate.

  • Follow the laboratory's established policies and procedures whenever test systems are not within the laboratory's established acceptable levels of performance.

  • Follow the laboratory's procedures for specimen handling and processing, test analyses, reporting and maintaining records of patient test results.

  • Fosters continued improvement in the quality of patient care by actively evaluating current work systems and suggesting or supporting positive changes.

  • Initiates, suggests, and if necessary, implements technical and administrative changes upon approval of appropriate technical coordinator.

  • Maintain records that demonstrate that proficiency testing samples are tested in the same manner as patient samples.

  • May assist the section supervisor in preparing and writing procedure manuals.

  • May calibrate instruments and assess the accuracy of the equipment; may perform first line preventive and corrective maintenance on equipment including optical, electronic and mechanical apparatus and may institute necessary service, in the absence of the section or shift supervisor, or as required by the supervisor.

  • May review all outgoing reports for technical and clerical errors as requested. Notifies the technical coordinator when supplies are at a low level.

  • Performs all routine and new test procedures which are complex and require professional judgment when assigned to a specific work area.

  • Performs patient responsibilities considering needs specific to the standard of care for patient's age.

  • Performs phlebotomy or assistance in the front office as necessary.

  • Promotes an atmosphere of professionalism and cooperation by interacting with others in a calm, courteous and helpful manner.

  • Provides accurate and timely test results by performing assigned tests in accordance with established procedures and policies.

  • Reads the results of tests and examinations and interprets them in terms of the quality of the test performed and definitiveness of the results as they relate to each other and to different age groups.

  • Recognized the administrative changes in staffing and scheduling and adapted to these changes.

  • Recognizes departures from a norm (for different age groups) and be able to understand the scientific and theoretical reasons for such deviation.

  • Responds to the needs of the department and hospital by performing other job-related duties as assigned.

Preferred (Not required) Microbiology experience, preferred.

title: Senior Employee Relations Specialist (6-month FTC)
description:
About InvestEngine

InvestEngine is everything the modern investor should need. Unbeatable value, market-leading automation, and built for easy, long-term investing. We've built a strong foundation, have over £3 billion invested, award-winning service, and a passionate team — now we're ready to scale.

As we grow, we want our approach to employee relations to be as clear, fair and consistent as everything else we build — so people always know where they stand, and managers always know how to do the right thing.

This is a build-and-enable role. You'll design the frameworks, policies and manager toolkits that make good people practice easy and predictable across the company, coach managers so everyday conversations happen early and well, and be a trusted, impartial point of support for both employees and managers when something needs working through.

It's deliberately senior and time-boxed: we want experienced judgement to set the foundations properly, so the capability stays with our managers and People team long after the six months are up.

This role is ideal for someone who's pragmatic, warm and commercially minded, and who enjoys building from a blank page rather than inheriting a large HR machine. You'll work closely with the People team, managers and senior leadership, with real autonomy to own employee relations end to end. This role is fully remote.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and embed our core employee relations framework: clear policies, manager playbooks, templates and decision guides across performance, conduct, grievance, absence and family leave

  • Review our people policies end to end and make them genuinely useful — updating them, adding supporting resources and manager guidance, and communicating changes well

  • Coach and enable managers so everyday conversations happen early, constructively and with confidence

  • Design and run practical manager training and workshops on feedback, wellbeing, absence, family leave and having supportive conversations

  • Act as an impartial, trusted adviser to employees and managers alike, helping resolve questions and concerns fairly and consistently

  • Support the full range of employee relations matters with care and confidentiality

  • Bring structure and consistency to how we record and handle people matters, so everyone is treated to the same standard

  • Use insight from themes and trends to prevent issues recurring and to improve the employee experience

  • Use AI tools to speed up drafting, research and policy work — pragmatically, and always within confidentiality limits

What We’re Looking For

  • Deep, hands-on employee relations experience, owning a range of people matters end to end and independently

  • Strong practical command of UK employment law and the ACAS Code

  • A calm, human approach to sensitive conversations, staying impartial and credible with employees and managers alike, and helping resolve things early and informally wherever possible

  • Excellent written work — clear, fair, well-structured documentation and communications

  • Track record of coaching managers and building their confidence through playbooks, training and in-the-moment support

  • Clear, human policy writing, and the discipline to use themes and insight to improve things rather than repeat them

  • Experience building in a lean environment without an ER centre of excellence or in-house legal team — comfortable with pace, ambiguity and a blank page

  • Sound judgement and impeccable handling of confidential information

Nice to Have

  • Background in fintech, financial services or high-growth scale-ups

  • Experience in an FCA-regulated (or similarly regulated) environment

  • Comfort living in workflow tools — building trackers, templates and automations rather than working through Word docs and email chains

  • Experience applying AI to ER drafting, case summarisation or policy research

How We Work

We're a ~180-person, AI-first fintech and a lean, fast-moving team that values clarity, ownership and transparency. You'll have the freedom to experiment, the responsibility to follow through, and the backing of a team that values clear thinking and open dialogue. We believe in solving problems at the root, not just treating the symptoms.

What We Offer

Impact from day one

A clearly defined 6-month mandate with visible impact on fairness, consistency and manager capability across the business.

Real ownership

This is the senior employee relations voice at InvestEngine. You'll shape the approach, build the frameworks, and leave behind something that lasts.

Transparent and open culture

We share decisions openly, keep communication channels clear, and encourage collaboration across every part of the business.

Supportive, high-calibre team

Work alongside talented professionals who are experts in their fields — smart, driven, and generous with their knowledge.

Remote and flexible

Fully remote. We focus on results, not rigid hours, and trust you to manage your time effectively.

Our Hiring Process

  1. Introductory call with our Talent team

  2. Skills interview — a deep dive into your experience, including a difficult-conversation and a manager-coaching scenario

  3. Gamified cognitive assessment to understand how you think and problem-solve

  4. Final interview with the hiring manager — working through real examples end to end, and alignment with our culture and values

title: SoC Power Validation Engineer
description:
The SOC hardware development team is looking for a motivated candidate to fill a full-time position. The primary role is to verify the integrity of the power grid. This includes setting the static IR drop and instantaneous voltage drop (IVD) targets for multiple SOCs and verifying that targets are met.

The main responsibility of this role is to provide initial assessment of power grids for new chips and new technology, define settings for power grid simulations, and verify power grid integrity. The candidate will be expected to: • Develop experimental flows for power integrity analysis tools using CAD flow — simulations include input from timing, package, and board level abstraction. • Drive initial assessment of static IR drop, instantaneous voltage drop (IVD), and power grid noise for jitter analysis in power grids. • Determine settings for SOC analysis for different types of grids, including electro-migration/IR/IVD analysis. • Work with physical design and timing teams to analyze simulation results, verify that power grid integrity targets are met, and enhance simulation flow. • Explore new tools and methodologies for power grid integrity.

Minimum Qualifications

  • A minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant field and a minimum of 3 years of relevant industry experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • The candidate should have experience in ASIC design methodology with an emphasis on power grid analysis.
  • Expert user of Redhawk, Voltus, or other equivalent power grid analysis tool.
  • Strong understanding of power grid integrity and reliability.
  • Experience in physical design implementation, STA preferred.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work on a team since the position requires interfacing with cross functional teams.
  • Experience in spice simulations and library characterization.
  • Good technical writing skills.
  • 3+ years of experience preferred.

title: HID Algorithms Engineer
description:
Apple's Human Interface Devices (HID) group develops innovative ways to interact with Apple products. We work on nearly every product line, delivering technologies like AirPods, iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other future Apple input technologies.

We're looking for an algorithms engineer to help build the next generation of human-computer interactions from the ground up. We are an eclectic group with backgrounds in computer science, controls, human factors, signal processing, and more. As a member of this team, you will work in the earliest stages of development, whether defining entirely new interactions or bringing new sensing technologies to life for the first time, making foundational decisions that determine how future Apple products are experienced.

As an Algorithms Engineer, you will prototype and define interactions end-to-end, investigating emerging technologies and new interaction paradigms in close collaboration with HW, SW, and design partners. You will develop and validate algorithmic concepts, and drive the technical work needed to bring these ideas to life. You will take prototypes from concept to production, writing code that ships in Apple products used by millions of people every year. You are self-motivated, comfortable operating in ambiguity, and quick to build relationships across disciplines. You thrive in the space where the problem isn't fully defined and the solution doesn't exist yet.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience in early-stage algorithm development, from concept through validation
  • Algorithm and mathematics fundamentals — state machine design, statistics, signal processing, machine learning, etc.
  • Experience programming in C++ and Python
  • Able to communicate clearly and collaborate with cross-functional teams
  • Excellent problem solving and root cause analysis skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • MS/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Human Computer Interaction, or related field / equivalent experience ; 5+ years of experience in a related field.
  • Experience developing for real-time systems

  • Experience developing software with agentic workflows

The Senior Functional and Automated Tester plans, designs, and executes functional and automated testing for modern applications, with a focus on quality, security, performance, and operational readiness. This role works closely with product, development, DevSecOps, and stakeholders to ensure solutions meet business requirements and are released with confidence. The tester leads test strategy and automation approaches, drives defect prevention through early engagement, and helps establish consistent testing standards across teams and projects.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT:

  • Lead or contribute to project planning by identifying testing scope, risks, environment needs, test data requirements, and tooling to support delivery timelines.
  • Translate business and technical requirements into test strategies, test plans, and detailed test cases, covering functional, integration, regression, performance, and security-related validation.
  • Design and build automated tests (unit, API, integration, and user interface) using a disciplined approach that supports repeatable and reliable execution within a continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline.
  • Perform hands-on functional testing of workflows, edge cases, data validations, and error handling; verify that solutions meet user and operational expectations.
  • Validate event/message-based services and distributed workflows, including systems that use message queues such as Apache Kafka, ensuring correct processing, resiliency, and traceability.
  • Test and validate API-centric and cloud-friendly designs (microservices, serverless applications), including backward compatibility, contract expectations, and integration with internal and external partners.
  • Partner with DevSecOps and engineering teams to ensure consistent application of development standards, procedures, and processes, including secure development expectations.
  • Support system compatibility and environment readiness by coordinating with technical teams on test environments, deployments, configuration changes, and release readiness.
  • Apply data security procedures in testing activities; identify potential data security risks and ensure defects and risks are documented, escalated, and tracked through resolution.
  • Produce and maintain clear testing documentation (test evidence, defect reports, dashboards, charts/diagrams, and runbooks as needed) suitable for leadership and audit reviews.
  • Drive defect triage and root-cause analysis with developers and stakeholders; verify fixes and help implement preventative quality controls.
  • Promote strong operational practices including observability validation (logging, metrics, tracing), performance baselines, and readiness checks.

Bring your expertise and drive for innovation to GDIT.

  • Experience testing API-centric architectures such as microservices and serverless applications, including contract validation and integration testing.
  • Cloud and data pipeline familiarity, including one or more of the following: Dataflow, Pub/Sub, Redis.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills, including analyzing logs/metrics/traces, isolating failures across components, and supporting defect triage.
  • Solid technical fluency in one or more languages used for test automation and validation, such as Java, Python, SQL, and/or JavaScript (and familiarity with modern web stacks such as React is a plus).

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to explain quality risks and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Experience working in Agile delivery teams and applying Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) practices.

description:
The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.


Meet the team:

As a Staff Vendor Management Analyst, you are responsible for supplier performance and relationship management across Dexcom’s global strategic suppliers and contract manufacturers. This role ensures continuity of supply, reduces vendor risks, improves vendor performance, maximize value and decreases costs. This is an advanced professional position that requires leadership of initiatives, strategic influence, and independent execution through cross-functional collaboration in driving results on quality, delivery, cost and services aligned with organizational objectives.

Where you come in:

  • Lead global strategic suppliers/CM governance and performance improvement initiatives
  • Influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership to resolve complex issues and implement best practices
  • Monitor and report supplier performance; collaborate with cross-functional teams in driving corrective actions
  • Collaborate and coordinate with Planning & Operations to align on CM build plan through CM S&OP process, monitor CM production/shipment performance and resolve supply issues
  • Coordinate cross‑functionally with Dexcom’s global factory teams to manage vendor supply and minimize potential disruptions to manufacturing operations
  • Drive cost reduction, VAVE and continuous improvement programs with measurable outcomes
  • Oversee supplier readiness for NPI and change management projects at CMs, ensuring compliance and timely execution
  • Provide executive level reporting/briefing at regular intervals on supplier performance, risks, mitigation and strategic opportunities
  • Contribute to process and policy development

What makes you successful:

  • Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 8-12 years of related experience.
  • Experience in managing supplier relationships
  • Familiar with S&OP process and MRP
  • Ability to effectively influence others and manage sensitive situations
  • Strong analytical, negotiation and communication skills
  • Ability to build and maintain strong stakeholder relationships with a collaborative mindset
  • Strong organizational and time management skills to meet deadlines
  • High competency in problem-solving and self-motivated to overcome challenges and obstacles

What you’ll get:

  • A front row seat to life changing CGM technology. Learn about our brave #dexcomwarriors community.
  • A full and comprehensive benefits program.
  • Growth opportunities on a global scale.
  • Access to career development through in-house learning programs and/or qualified tuition reimbursement.
  • An exciting and innovative, industry-leading organization committed to our employees, customers, and the communities we serve.

Travel Required:

  • 15-25%

Dexcom is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes/applications.

title: Service Detail Technician - AutoNation Honda Tucson Mall

title: Associate Distribution Engineer
description:
Job Description

Leidos is seeking an Associate Distribution Engineer in our Minneapolis, MN office.

*** This position would require the selected candidate to work through our contractor with the possibility of converting to direct employment with Leidos approximately 6 months after start date.***

The successful candidate will have an interest in developing construction work packages for the electric distribution system using various software systems and construction standards. Distribution systems may be in an OH, UG, or URD environment. Project work may include grid hardening and reliability, substation optimization, joint use make ready and street light projects. Work packages will be developed using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Computer Aided Design (CAD) tools, Work Management Systems (WMS), and other client systems. Project work will require performing engineering calculations that may include: structural analysis of poles, guying, cable pulling, electric demand, fault currents, and coordination of protective devices. Assignments may also include: preparing forestry trimming requests, facilitating permit and Right-of-Way acquisition, development of a BOM, estimating costs, and customer advocacy such as acquiring easements.

In this role, you can also expect to gain experience/expertise in:

  • NESC expertise

  • Structural Pole Modeling

  • Electrical Power Calculations

  • GIS Design

  • Interactions with other disciplines (Substation, Protection & Controls, and Civil Structural)

The successful Associate Distribution Engineer candidate will support the following activities under supervision of a technical lead:

  • Develop design and construction work packages for electrical overhead and underground distribution systems operating from 4kV through 138kV mostly associated with programmatic work such as overloaded transformers, inspection and maintenance, joint use, and inspection reports.

  • Comply with Leidos and Client Safety requirements as well as design and quality expectations.

  • Travel to sites as needed, perform inspections and return to the office to perform engineering design work.

  • Perform engineering calculations such as: structural analysis for wood pole loading, guying calculations, specifying conductor sags and tensions for recommended spans, and calculation of voltage drop and flicker.

  • Develop permitting documents for different AHJ’s.

  • Provide engineering support during construction, including post-construction reviews to ensure all applicable engineering and construction standards have been met.

  • Conduct root cause analysis of outages and mitigation using engineering principles and design.

Successful candidates can look forward to a fast paced, diverse work environment and flexible work hours/work arrangements as well as managers who will encourage career development and growth including:

  • Engineer in Training Certificate (EIT)

  • Professional Engineer Licensure (PE)

  • Project Management Professional (PMP)

  • Technical & Non-Technical Training Opportunities

  • Leadership Training

  • Opportunity to Lead, Grow, and Inspire a Dynamic Team

Associate Distribution Engineer Basic Qualifications:

  • Requires BS Degree from an ABET accredited Engineering program and 6-24 months of prior relevant electric utility distribution experience

  • Experience with NESC Standards, ESRI, AutoCAD and/or MicroStation, and GIS a plus.

  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.) required.

  • Excellent verbal and written communications skills.

  • Willingness to perform both field and office work.

  • Overnight travel may be required (10-20% travel).

  • Ability to work in outdoor environments.

  • Ability to utilize personal vehicle.

No two career paths will ever look the same. At Leidos, we know the most talented and diverse engineering professionals will always have a multitude of career choices; your time at Leidos will be a wise investment in your career and in yourself.

Leidos is a trusted and technology-focused solutions provider. Utilities and mobile operators rely on our Power Delivery Services Team for reliable power and telecommunication expertise, as reflected through our work with more than 50 investor-owned utilities, more than 160 municipals/cooperatives, as well as a growing number of mobile operators, local utility providers and private developers. In addition to providing engineering and project management services, Leidos works with an established group of industry-leading construction partners delivering meaningful Energy Delivery Solutions. Our recognition as an industry leader is confirmed by the latest national rankings by Engineering News-Record (ENR) ranking Leidos within the Top 10 T&D Firms, and Top 10 Power Firms.

PDSDLINE

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

title: Lead  Software Engineer(Python/AWS/SQL)
description:
Job Description Summary

Roles at Lead IC level solve complex problems and guide others through code, design, and architecture. Scope includes
owning technical direction and architecture in a defined area, mentoring peers, and raising quality through reuse and hands-on
support. The impact is consistent, high-quality solutions that reduce duplication and accelerate team delivery.​

## ROLE SUMMARY

Are you a software developer who loves building software that actually gets used?

Join us at FTSE Russell! We're building a team of engineers who care about software craftsmanship, clean code, and shipping things that matter. As a Software Engineer, you'll build the services, libraries, and applications that power the indices trusted by financial institutions worldwide.

We work primarily in Python, so that's our preference — but we care far more about whether you can genuinely build software than about which language you built it in. If your track record is in Java, C#, C, C++, Scala, Go, or Rust and you're keen to work in Python, we want to hear from you. Strong engineers pick up a new language quickly; strong engineering judgement takes years.

This is a hands-on software development role. You'll spend your days designing, coding, testing, and shipping — in a modern AWS environment, alongside engineers who review each other's code, pair when it helps, and take real ownership of what they build. The systems you work on handle serious volumes of financial data, so there's a rich data dimension to the problems — but the craft we're hiring for is software engineering.

If you've built real software and want to keep building, we'd love to meet you.

## WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

We're building the next-generation index data platform at FTSE Russell — and we want you to help build it:

Looking for 10+yrs of experience in writing production code, primarily in Python — services, APIs, libraries, and command-line tools that are modular, well-tested, and built to be maintained by others
- Designing and building software components end to end, from breaking down a problem through to deployment and support in production
- Applying modern software engineering practices every day: version control, trunk-based development, CI/CD, code review, refactoring, and automated testing (unit, integration, contract)
- Taking ownership of features and systems — you debug your own problems, fix them properly, and take responsibility for the quality of what you deliver
- Designing data models and integrations across relational databases (Aurora PostgreSQL) and object storage, thinking carefully about schema design, evolution, and backwards compatibility
- Building software that processes data at scale on AWS — Lambda, S3, containerised services, and where appropriate the AWS data stack (Glue, EMR Serverless)
- Building observability in from the start — structured logging, metrics, tracing, and meaningful alerting, so that we know how our software behaves in production
- Contributing to design and architecture discussions, and to our shared engineering standards
- Working directly with product and business teams to turn requirements into working software
- Learning the financial indices domain and sharing what you learn with the team

## WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Essential — this is the bar:

- You have built and shipped real software. Not scripts and notebooks — applications, services, or libraries that other people depended on, that you maintained and evolved over time
- Python is our preference, but not a hard gate. Either you already write strong production Python, or you have that depth in another serious general-purpose language — Java, C#, C, C++, Scala, Go, or Rust — and are genuinely motivated to work in Python here. We'll give you the time and support to get fluent
- You write clean, maintainable, testable, extensible code. In Python that means type hints, linters and formatters (ruff, mypy, black), and a genuine testing habit with pytest; we'd expect the equivalent discipline in whatever language you've come from
- Strong software engineering fundamentals — modular design, sensible abstractions, dependency management, packaging, error handling, and knowing when *not* to add a layer
- You are hands-on and want to stay hands-on. You enjoy being in the code
- Practical experience with Git-based workflows, code review, and CI/CD
- Strong experience with relational databases (e.g. Aurora PostgreSQL) — schema design, query writing, and understanding what happens under the hood
- Working knowledge of a cloud platform, ideally AWS (S3, Lambda, containers, IAM basics)
- You're comfortable with data-shaped problems — batch processing, ETL, schema evolution — or you're keen to learn them
- You enjoy the business context and working closely with stakeholders rather than at arm's length
- You work well in Agile teams and value collaboration over solo heroics

## NICE TO HAVES

Great if you bring these, but we'll happily teach you:

- Apache Spark / PySpark or other large-scale distributed processing
- Big data experience — working with datasets and workloads that don't fit on one machine
- Additional languages used in data-intensive software — Scala, Java, C++, Go, or Rust — particularly where you've used them for performance-sensitive or high-throughput work
- Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or similar open table formats, and lakehouse architecture
- Databricks, Snowflake, or comparable data platforms
- CI/CD tooling such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, or GitHub Actions
- Infrastructure as code (Terraform, CDK)
- Data quality frameworks like Great Expectations or Deequ
- Curiosity about financial markets, index data, or investment analytics
- Experience in finance domain (investment banking, asset/portfolio management) or in any product company

---

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to build software that matters, we'd love to hear from you.

Career Stage:

Manager

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Information:

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a significant impact, we'd love to hear from you.

LSEG is a leading global financial markets infrastructure and data provider. Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth.

Our purpose is the foundation on which our culture is built. Our values of Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change underpin our purpose and set the standard for everything we do, every day. They go to the heart of who we are and guide our decision making and everyday actions.

Working with us means that you will be part of a dynamic organisation of 25,000 people across 65 countries. However, we will value your individuality and enable you to bring your true self to work so you can help enrich our diverse workforce.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. This means that we do not discriminate on the basis of anyone’s race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. Conforming with applicable law, we can reasonably accommodate applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs.

You will be part of a collaborative and creative culture where we encourage new ideas. We are committed to sustainability across our global business and we are proud to partner with our customers to help them meet their sustainability objectives. Our charity, the LSEG Foundation provides charitable grants to community groups that help people access economic opportunities and build a secure future with financial independence. Colleagues can get involved through fundraising and volunteering.

LSEG offers a range of tailored benefits and support, including healthcare, retirement planning, paid volunteering days and wellbeing initiatives.

title: Test Technician
description:
Be visionary

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.​

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

Job Description

**$2,000 sign-on bonus for qualified individuals**

Our facility in Exton, Pennsylvania is home to the Solidtron Advanced Thyristor Products Business Unit. This facility offers a diverse technical team with expertise in the design, packaging, assembly, testing and application support for a broad gamut of state-of-the-art and next-generation pulsed-power semiconductor components and high-power switch assemblies.

Job Summary:
Teledyne Qioptiq has an immediate need for a Test Technician. This is a non-exempt position that would receive overtime for working over 40 hours in a week. Our ideal candidate is self-motivated, able to perform duties with minimal supervision, thrives on challenge, mastering new information and ideas, is innovative and flexible, willing to tackle any task required in a constantly changing environment, can grow intellectually and professionally along with our company

Responsibilities:

  • Perform repetitive standard electrical voltage tests for a high-volume product line;
  • Tests are performed on controlled, calibrated test equipment to designated test routers;
  • Determines proper test set-ups, tests, troubleshoots, and notifies appropriate personnel when problems arise as necessary;
  • Performs other related duties of comparable complexity as directed.
  • Data capture and compilation both manually and electronically
  • Tasks/process steps are to be completed according to schedule

Requirements:

  • Requires a high school diploma or equivalent and specialized training beyond high school usually acquired with six to twenty-four (6-24) months of industrial experience;
  • Pays attention to fine details;
  • Can perform repetitive tasks with attentiveness;
  • Can handle and manipulate small parts with hands and tweezers under microscopes, steady hands are a must;
  • Has basic mathematical skills, specifically can read and interpret graphs;
  • Can follow precisely controlled procedures and instructions as presented (written and verbal);
  • Has basic knowledge of computers and electronics, semiconductor knowledge is a plus;
  • Organized, neat, and orderly;
  • Team player;
  • Good communication skills;
  • The ability to prioritize and switch between tasks as necessary;
  • Experience with work environment Outlook, MS Office, and MRP programs is a plus.
  • Please note that due to the requirements from the Department of Energy, U.S. CITIZENSHIP IS REQUIRED;

Desirable Skills:

  • Knowledge of electrical and electronic theory (Ohms law, electrical formulas…etc.);
  • Practical working knowledge of electronic test equipment to include Oscilloscopes, multi-meters, curve-tracers, power supplies and pulse/signal generators;

title: Program Manager, Owner Experience
description:
Job Description

The Program Manager, Owner Experience serves as a subject matter expert in Mazda's Omotenashi philosophy and is responsible for translating strategic priorities into programs and initiatives that strengthen dealer adoption, enhance the owner experience, and support reail excellence across the dealer network. Working independently and in partnership with dealer leadership, field teams, Retail Operations, Training, and cross-functional stakeholders, this role develops, implements, and sustains programs that drive engagement, capability building, recognition, best-practice sharing, and continuous improvement to foster a customer-centric culture and long-term business results.

Major Responsibilities
  • (60%) Omotenashi Program Management & Enablement
    • Drive Owner Experience and Omotenashi initiatives from concept through implementation; inclusive of program design, plans, roadmaps, budgets, timelines, milestones, and success metrics
    • Develop and implement tools, resources, frameworks, and best practices that help dealerships operationalize Mazda’s Omotenashi philosophy and Behavioral Framework
    • Execute communications strategies and engagement plans that drive awareness, participation, and adoption of Omotenashi initiatives throughout the dealer network
    • Create dealer-facing communications related to Omotenashi activations, ambassador engagement, workshops, leadership forums, recognition programs, and new initiatives
    • Deliver dealer recognition initiatives that celebrate achievements, reinforce desired behaviors, and showcase impactful Omotenashi implementation
    • Design and develop executive presentations, facilitation materials, implementation guides, business cases, dealer resources, communication campaigns, and support materials
    • Partner with Retail Operations, Regions, Field Teams, CRM, Training, Marketing, HR, and other business functions to embed Omotenashi principles into existing programs, tools, and processes
    • Support internal MNAO adoption of Omotenashi principles through communications, storytelling, engagement activities, and cross-functional collaboration
    • Champion Omotenashi through presentations and facilitation for dealer, regional, and internal audiences
    • Identify program risks, barriers, and opportunities; implement solutions to support successful outcomes
  • (25%) Dealer Engagement
    • Drive initiatives that expand, strengthen, and sustain Mazda’s dealer community
    • Develop engagement strategies for dealership Omotenashi Ambassadors and dealer leadership
    • Coordinate and facilitate dealer activations, ambassador workshops, leadership Forums, networking opportunities, peer-learning events, and community-building activities
    • Build strong relationships with dealer leaders, ambassadors, area experience managers, and regional teams to drive participation and long-term engagement
    • Support dealer onboarding and activation efforts by developing implementation resources, engagement plans, and sustainment strategies
    • Partner with regional teams to identify opportunities to increase dealer participation and elevate dealer performance
    • Identify, document, and share dealership best practices that support broader adoption throughout the Mazda network
    • Capture dealer feedback, challenges, and emerging needs to continuously improve Omotenashi initiatives and engagement strategies
  • (15%) Metrics Development & Continuous Improvement
    • Develop measurement strategies evaluating dealer engagement, adoption, effectiveness, and business impact of Omotenashi initiatives
    • Establish and monitor key performance indicators for Ambassador engagement, dealership participation, community growth, activation progress, communications effectiveness, and recognition efforts
    • Analyze qualitative and quantitative feedback from dealers, Ambassadors, field teams, and owners to identify trends, opportunities, and barriers to adoption
    • Develop executive reporting, dashboards, presentations, and strategic recommendations that translate insights into action
    • Measure the effectiveness of workshops, forums, resources, communications, activation efforts, and dealer engagement activities while identifying opportunities for improvement
    • Partner with cross-functional teams to connect Omotenashi initiatives to owner experience, customer satisfaction, dealer performance, retention, and loyalty outcomes
    • Identify emerging trends, innovative approaches, and best practices that strengthen Mazda’s owner experience and retail culture

title: Senior System/Network Administrator – Systems Integration
description:
About Leidos

Leidos is a FORTUNE 500® company bringing a mix of innovative technology and sector expertise to customers in the national security, engineering, and health industries. We deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers' success. Guided by our Mission, Vision, and Values, Leidos empowers its teams, contributes to its communities, and operates sustainably—always with a commitment to doing the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community.

The Leidos Intel Sector combines technology-enabled services and mission software capabilities to support Intelligence Community customers as they address evolving national security challenges.

About the Opportunity

Leidos is seeking a highly experienced Senior System/Network Administrator – Systems Integration to support the implementation, operation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of complex IT systems and infrastructure.

You will administer Linux, UNIX, and Windows environments; build and maintain virtual and storage environments; configure network components; resolve complex technical problems; and support reliable day-to-day infrastructure operations. At this level, you will also contribute to system and mission-architecture design, understand system-administration interdependencies within Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) environments, and resolve complex integration issues spanning server hardware, applications, and software.

Why This Role Matters

Mission infrastructure depends not only on the reliability of individual systems, networks, storage platforms, and virtual environments, but also on how those components interact as part of a larger architecture.

As a Senior System/Network Administrator – Systems Integration, you will bring deep infrastructure experience to both operational administration and complex integration challenges, helping ensure interconnected systems and applications function effectively together.

What You'll Do

Systems, Network & Infrastructure Administration

  • Manage daily configuration and operation of IT systems.

  • Support implementation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of IT systems and associated infrastructure.

  • Monitor and support day-to-day operations across client/server, storage, network, mobile, and related devices.

  • Configure and manage Linux, UNIX, Windows, and other applicable operating systems.

  • Install and load operating-system software, troubleshoot system issues, and maintain system integrity.

  • Configure network components and implement operating-system enhancements to improve reliability and performance.

  • Build, configure, monitor, and maintain virtual environments.

  • Build, configure, monitor, and maintain storage environments.

  • Optimize system operations and resource utilization and perform system-capacity analysis and planning.

Advanced Troubleshooting & User Support

  • Provide in-depth troubleshooting of IT systems.

  • Assist users in accessing and using IT systems.

  • Provide Tier 1 Help Desk and Tier 2 escalation support for problem identification, diagnosis, and resolution.

  • Support dispatch-system and hardware problems and remain engaged through resolution.

  • Provide detailed analysis and feedback to agency management and internal customers for escalated tickets.

  • Communicate system status, technical issues, and resolution progress to agency management and internal customers.

Systems Integration & Mission Architecture

  • Support the design of systems, mission architecture, and associated hardware.

  • Apply working knowledge of system-administration interdependencies within Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) environments.

  • Analyze and resolve complex problems involving server hardware, applications, and software integration.

Required Qualifications

Clearance

  • Active TS/SCI with Polygraph, at time of Application, to be considered for the position.

Education & Experience

  • Fifteen (15) years of System/Network Administration experience supporting programs and contracts of similar scope, type, and complexity.

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline from an accredited college or university.

  • Five (5) additional years of System/Network Administration experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree.

description:

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Pest Control Technicians do?

The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for residential customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points

  • Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards

  • Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Provide advice on how to reduce the risk of future infestations.

  • Build relationships with customers, schedule and confirm their appointments, help with sales to current customers, and expand our product to new customers

  • Ensure that all pest control equipment is properly maintained, stocked, and in good working condition

  • Adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations regarding pest control products and safety protocols

  • Drive and safely operate a company provided service vehicle (we provide routine maintenance)

Essential Job Functions:

  • Working in tight, confined spaces such as basements, attics, crawl spaces, narrow aisles, or passageways

  • Working around animals, insects and termites

  • You’ll sometimes be working around mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, heights and scaffolding, fumes, dust, and chemicals, and we’ll train you how to handle all of these conditions safely

  • Able to work both inside and outside in your local climate in company-provided weather gear

  • Lots of moving around — regularly sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, up and down stairs, ladders, scaffolding, ramps, and poles

  • You’ll need to wear personal protective equipment (PPE), like an OSHA-compliant respirator

What do you need?

  • Clean shaven face- for safety reasons (rebreathers have to be able to seal your face)

  • High school diploma or GED; related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience

  • Possess a valid driver’s license from state of residence.

  • Licenses/certificates as required by federal, state, and/or local regulations (covered by us)

  • Available to work Monday-Friday and weekends as needed

  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in all areas of pest control

  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills

  • Basic math skills — You’ll need to be able to follow instructions for mixing on product labels

  • Customer-facing experience preferred

Leidos has a new and exciting opportunity for a Mid/Sr Manual Test Engineer in our Intel Sector's Cyber & Analytics Business Area (CABA). Leidos has an exciting opportunity for a Mid/Sr Manual Test Engineer on an important, fast-paced, mission critical program. The selected candidate will perform component, integration, and system level testing by writing and executing system-level test procedures, evaluating changes made to software applications, and verifying defect corrective actions discovered during development, testing, and/or operational use.   • Must have experience collaborating with software developers to create formal test procedures.

  • Must have experience working with physical equipment in a test lab environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

title: Senior Director of Regulatory Advocacy
company: The League of Credit Unions & Affiliates
description:
The League of Credit Unions & Affiliates (The League) is seeking a full-time Senior Director of Regulatory Advocacy to join our Advocacy team. If you have strong political acumen, excellent communication skills, and the ability to navigate complex policy issues in a fast-paced environment, we want to hear from you! We're looking for someone who can exercise sound independent judgment, manage competing priorities and deadlines, and successfully lead projects both independently and collaboratively.

This opportunity is ideal for an experienced compliance or government affairs professional who is organized, adaptable, and passionate about advocating for the interests of credit unions.

As the Senior Director of Regulatory Advocacy, you will work closely with our regulatory advocacy team, state and federal lobbyists, and compliance team to strategically engage regulatory agencies and policymakers. You will help ensure credit unions are represented, informed, and influential in the development of laws and regulations affecting the industry.

What You'll Take Ownership Of:

  • Representing The League before state and federal agency officials, building trusted relationships across both political parties.
  • Monitoring and analyzing federal legislation, committee hearings, and regulatory proposals to identify threats and opportunities for credit unions.
  • Reviewing proposed bills and providing analysis of credit union impact to state lobbyists and member credit unions.
  • Drafting policy briefs, position statements, and testimony to support The League's positions on federal issues such as Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) rulemakings, National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) regulations, and IRS- and tax-related matters.
  • Coordinating with national trade associations and federal partners to align messaging and strengthen industry-wide influence.
  • Supporting the development and execution of state-level advocacy strategies across The League's footprint, including attending policy meetings and providing written policy analysis.
  • Contributing to The League's comment letters, regulatory alerts, and grassroots calls-to-action on both state and federal issues.
  • Assisting with advocacy events such as "Hike the Hill," state legislative events, and regulatory roundtables, including preparation of briefing materials and participant coordination.
  • Engaging with member credit unions to educate and mobilize them around key advocacy priorities, including grassroots efforts and PAC engagement.
  • Serving as a liaison to select regulatory agencies, including the CFPB, NCUA, and state regulators, as needed, building and maintaining relationships with key agency contacts on credit union issues.
  • Performing other duties and special projects as assigned.

What You'll Bring to the Role:

  1. Bachelor's degree in political science, public policy, or a related field is required. A Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school is a plus.
  2. Five years of experience in legislative affairs, regulatory advocacy, public policy, or compliance, preferably in a trade association, Capitol Hill, or financial services setting.
  3. Demonstrated experience lobbying or engaging with federal and/or state government officials, with a track record of advancing policy or regulatory outcomes.
  4. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Outlook, as well as Salesforce or a similar CRM platform.

Work Schedule:

The Senior Director of Regulatory Advocacy will be required to travel up to 50% across The League's footprint-including Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Virginia, Washington, D.C., state capitals, and member credit unions. Overnight travel is likely and a valid driver's license is required.

How to Apply:

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, please complete our brief online application, which takes less than five minutes. After submitting your application, you'll receive a link to complete a short assessment. Both steps are required to move forward in the hiring process.

Why Work at The League?

The League provides a platform for advocacy, collaboration, and innovation, representing nearly 400 credit unions in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, and Virginia and their more than 33 million members and over $467 billion in assets. The League advances and supports credit unions through advocacy, engagement, Foundation resources, and LEVERAGE products and services.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a team member-centric culture, offering competitive salaries, and providing exceptional benefits. Our comprehensive benefits package includes:

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life and long-term disability coverage
  • Flexible spending account
  • Generous paid time off and volunteer time off
  • 14 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan with company match
  • Professional development funding and tuition reimbursement

At The League, we prioritize a strong workplace culture, work-life balance, and meaningful team member engagement while staying dedicated to our mission of supporting credit unions and the communities they serve

The League enforces a drug-free workplace policy and employment offers are contingent on drug-screen and background check.
