title: Pest Control Technician
description:
Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period!

For more information about our benefits, see below!

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Pest Control Technicians do?

The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for residential customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points

  • Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards

  • Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Provide advice on how to reduce the risk of future infestations.

  • Build relationships with customers, schedule and confirm their appointments, help with sales to current customers, and expand our product to new customers

  • Ensure that all pest control equipment is properly maintained, stocked, and in good working condition

  • Adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations regarding pest control products and safety protocols

  • Drive and safely operate a company provided service vehicle (we provide routine maintenance)

Essential Job Functions:

  • Working in tight, confined spaces such as basements, attics, crawl spaces, narrow aisles, or passageways

  • Working around animals, insects and termites

  • You’ll sometimes be working around mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, heights and scaffolding, fumes, dust, and chemicals, and we’ll train you how to handle all of these conditions safely

  • Able to work both inside and outside in your local climate in company-provided weather gear

  • Lots of moving around — regularly sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, up and down stairs, ladders, scaffolding, ramps, and poles

  • You’ll need to wear personal protective equipment (PPE), like an OSHA-compliant respirator

What do you need?

  • Clean shaven face- for safety reasons (rebreathers have to be able to seal your face)

  • High school diploma or GED; related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience

  • Must possess a valid driver's license from state of residence (Company vehicle and gas card provided)

  • Licenses/certificates as required by federal, state, and/or local regulations (covered by us)

  • Available to work Monday-Friday and weekends as needed

  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in all areas of pest control

  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills

  • Basic math skills — You’ll need to be able to follow instructions for mixing on product labels

  • Customer-facing experience preferred

A career with the Rentokil family of companies can be a professional trajectory filled with opportunity. We pride ourselves on being a world-class team that rewards high performance, and we love to promote from within. We offer competitive pay and many of our roles offer performance incentives.

description:
Whether you’re a recent grad or a seasoned professional, you can experience meaningful career growth at Rosendin. Enjoy a true sense of ownership as you work with a proven industry leader on some of the most exciting and high-profile projects in the nation. We offer a wide range of job opportunities, competitive compensation, full benefits, an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and more.

Why Rosendin?

Committed. Innovative. Engaged.

If you’re looking to take your career to the next level and work with some of the best and brightest in the industry, we want to hear from you. Since our founding over 100+ years ago, Rosendin has been driven to positively impact the communities where we live and work. We are an organization built on integrity and we have a culture that empowers people, embraces diversity, and inspires everyone to do their best. As one of the largest EMPLOYEE-OWNED electrical contractors in the United States, you will have the unique benefit of being a shareholder at a company that is experiencing tremendous growth and success. When our people succeed and fuel our success, we reward them. We'd love to have you as a shareholder!

YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY:

The Project Manager I is a mid-level project management position responsible for overseeing projects from planning through completion and ensuring client satisfaction by delivering unparalleled service. Provides overall project management support for several small to medium projects or one large project supporting senior project management.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Plan and organize a project under the direction of a Senior Project Manager and/or Division Manager.

  • Supervise and direct project activities, including assigning tasks to Assistant Project Managers, planning, coordinating, circumventing/resolving problem areas, and maintaining all company/project policies, procedures, standards, etc.

  • Provide project management expertise to establish initial client contact. This will include the assessment of the scope of work, schedule, and resources necessary to complete a project successfully.

  • Responsible for preparing a complete estimate for the selected project with a detailed review of plans, specifications, and bid form.

  • Establish project objectives, policies, procedures, and performance standards within the guidelines of corporate policies.

  • Supervise the preparation of all change orders on the project. Negotiate all change orders on the project.

  • Monitor construction activities with the onsite Foreman and Area Superintendent to ensure the project is built on schedule and within budget.

  • Investigate potentially serious situations and implement corrective measures within company guidelines and under supervision.

  • Supervise the preparation of all change quotations for presentation to the prime client and assist in negotiating all change quotations to a conclusion.

  • Prepare monthly costing reports under the supervision of a Senior PM or Division Manager.

  • Manage financial aspects of contracts (progress billing, rental equipment, income/expenses) to protect the company’s interest and simultaneously maintain good relationships with the client.

  • Review any documentation prepared by Assistant Project Manager before submission.

  • Represent the company in project meetings under the guidance of PM II or Sr. Project Manager.

  • The duties and responsibilities describe this position's general nature and scope of work. This is a partial listing, and other responsibilities will be assigned based on the position’s role within the

  • business unit.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL:

  • Ability to perform duties in a professional manner and appearance

  • Effective performance management skills

  • Extensive knowledge of safety protocols and procedures

  • Proficient in using a computer and Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.); Accubid and Oracle preferred

  • Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, changing priorities as necessary

  • Work under pressure and adapt to changing requirements with a positive attitude

  • Oral and written communication skills as required for the position

  • Self-motivated, proactive, and an effective team player

  • Interact effectively and professionally with all levels of employees, both management and staff alike, vendors, clients, and others

WHAT YOU BRING TO US:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or other related discipline preferred

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in the construction industry in a Project Management role

  • Can be a combination of training, education, and relevant work experience

TRAVEL:

  • Up to 25%

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • General work environment – This position is performed primarily on active construction sites. Activity includes sitting for extended periods, standing, walking, typing, carrying, pushing, bending. Work is conducted primarily indoors with varying environmental conditions, such as fluorescent lighting and air conditioning.

  • Noise level is typically low to medium.

  • Occasional lifting of up to 30 lbs.

  • We fully comply with the ADA and applicable state law, including considering reasonable accommodation measures that may enable qualified disabled applicants and employees to perform essential functions. YOU Matter – Our Benefits

title: Digital Solutions Business Partner (Panama City, Panama)
description:
Job Title

Digital Solutions Business Partner (Panama City, Panama)

Job Description

The Digital Solutions Business Partner leads the technology-enabled productivity agenda for their assigned business area. This role combines business insight, technology knowledge, and change leadership to translate strategic priorities and operational challenges into scalable digital solutions.

Working closely with business leaders, technology teams, regional stakeholders, and external partners, this position ensures that technology initiatives are aligned with business objectives and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, efficiency, and operational performance.

Your Role

  • Serve as the strategic partner between business units and technology teams, translating business priorities and operational challenges into scalable digital solutions.

  • Lead the identification, design, and implementation of technology-enabled solutions that improve productivity, efficiency, and business performance.

  • Develop and manage a portfolio of complex digital initiatives, including project scope, priorities, budgets, resources, risks, dependencies, and governance.

  • Partner with regional leaders, business stakeholders, IT teams, and external partners to gather requirements, develop roadmaps, and drive cross-functional execution.

  • Lead change management, solution adoption, validation testing, user acceptance testing, and continuous improvement while measuring and communicating business impact.

You’re the Right Fit If:

  • You have a bachelor’s degree in information technology, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • You have a minimum 8 years of experience in technology leadership, digital transformation, or a related area, including close collaboration with business units and regional stakeholders, Including demonstrated experience managing multiple complex projects or automation initiatives applying process improvement methodologies, such as value stream mapping, design thinking, Lean Six Sigma, Agile or comparable frameworks.

  • You have strong business acumen, leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate business needs into technology-enabled solutions and influence across organizational levels.

  • Your skills include Advanced English level (C1); deep knowledge of AI, machine learning, or Generative AI concepts; Familiarity with AI tools or services such as Azure AI, Copilot Studio; hands-on experience with Power Apps, Power Automate, or similar low-code tools; Understanding of APIs, data handling, and application integration concepts.

​

How we work together
We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

This is an office role. No company relocation benefits will be provided for this role, candidates must be based in Panama City, Panama.

Job Description:

Own your opportunity to shape the future of AI at GDIT
As an Agentic AI Engineer supporting the mission of the United States Postal Service (USPS), you will design, develop, and deploy AI solutions that modernize and optimize essential nationwide operations. Your work will directly contribute to improved efficiency, automated processes, and data‑driven decision making across a high‑impact federal environment.

MEANINGFUL WORK & PERSONAL IMPACT
You will play a critical role in identifying where AI can streamline business processes and deliver measurable outcomes across USPS. Support may include expertise in AI strategy, generative AI, machine learning, large language models, agentic AI, automation, analytics, governance, software engineering, architecture, and enterprise operational support.

Agentic AI & Architecture

  • Design and develop autonomous AI agents capable of reasoning, planning, and executing multi‑step workflows.
  • Create agent‑based architectures using orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, AutoGen, and similar technologies.
  • Build modular APIs, integrations, tools, and memory management capabilities, including vector database integration, to support intelligent agent operations.
  • Integrate AI solutions with existing enterprise automation frameworks to reduce manual effort and enhance operational quality.
  • Identify opportunities for AI‑enabled automation, operational efficiencies, productivity improvements, and modernization across USPS workflows.

ML/LLM Engineering

  • Demonstrate ability to design, build, train, deploy, integrate, and maintain machine learning and LLM‑based solutions.
  • Develop AI‑enabled automation solutions that improve business processes and support SDLC activities including coding, testing, debugging, deployment, and operational support.
  • Build tools that automate requirements and test case generation using Visual Studio Code, Python, Microsoft Copilot, CrewAI, or other USPS‑approved platforms.
  • Provide actionable recommendations, solution strategies, and operational insights to improve organizational performance and mission outcomes.

MLOps, Platforms & Performance

  • Implement MLOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, containerization technologies, and scalable deployment environments to support enterprise AI operations.
  • Establish evaluation and testing pipelines to measure AI accuracy, reliability, performance, scalability, and operational effectiveness.
  • Provide deep AI technical expertise to troubleshoot, diagnose, optimize, and maintain advanced AI systems, machine learning models, and production AI environments.
  • Optimize AI model performance, scalability, efficiency, and accuracy using tools such as PyTorch and TensorFlow.

Data & Analytics

  • Ensure data quality, integrity, governance, and security for AI model training, evaluation, deployment, and sustainment.
  • Support the collection, preprocessing, analysis, visualization, and reporting of largescale structured and structured datasets.
  • Develop dashboards, reports, predictive analytics, and executive‑level visualizations to support decision‑making and operational planning.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Develop and implement AI governance frameworks, policies, security controls, ethical AI standards, transparency mechanisms, and compliance processes.
  • Ensure compliance with cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory, and organizational requirements applicable to AI systems and enterprise environments.
  • Monitor, assess, and mitigate risks associated with AI deployment, automation, and enterprise integration.
  • Support executive leadership with AI strategic advisory services, roadmap development, assessments, briefings, and stakeholder engagement.

Collaboration, Enablement & Mission Outcomes

title: Systems Engineer – Sustainment Engineering & Digital Thread
description:
Leidos's Digital Sector is seeking a Systems Engineer-Sustainment Engineer and Digital Thread to support the U.S. Coast Guard CG-TECH-DME organization in executing enterprise digital transformation, sustainment engineering, and digital engineering initiatives supporting Force Design 2028 objectives. The Senior Systems Engineer will provide technical leadership in sustainment engineering, product lifecycle management (PLM), and digital thread management across enterprise transformation activities, modernization efforts, and mission enablement initiatives. The role will support planning, coordination, analysis, implementation, and governance activities associated with sustaining Coast Guard systems across their full lifecycle (from requirements and design through fielding, sustainment, and disposal) with authoritative, model-based data connecting every phase.

This individual will work closely with Coast Guard leadership, program managers, product line managers, enterprise architects, logisticians, cybersecurity teams, and mission stakeholders to define sustainment and technical requirements, establish and govern the digital thread, and ensure alignment between operational readiness needs and enterprise engineering objectives.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide sustainment-focused systems engineering support for Coast Guard digital transformation and lifecycle modernization initiatives, including reliability, maintainability, availability, and supportability analyses that inform readiness and total ownership cost decisions.

  • Establish, manage, and govern digital thread linkages connecting requirements, architecture models, engineering designs, configuration baselines, technical data, and sustainment/logistics data across the system lifecycle.

  • Administer, configure, and champion adoption of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software (e.g., Arras Innovator, PTC Windchill, Siemens Teamcenter), including workflows, change management processes, BOM/product structure management, and integrations with engineering and logistics systems.

  • Support configuration management and technical data management activities, including engineering change proposals, configuration audits, baseline control, and technical data package (TDP) development and maintenance within the PLM environment.

  • Analyze operational and sustainment requirements and develop technical recommendations supporting enterprise modernization and lifecycle support objectives.

  • Develop systems engineering artifacts including CONOPS, requirements documentation, interface definitions, sustainment plans, workflows, and technical assessments.

  • Translate operational requirements and concepts of operations into traceable UAFML model artifacts that support digital engineering, sustainment planning, and architecture decision-making.

  • Build and maintain enterprise and system architecture models in Cameo Enterprise Architecture, including diagrams, elements, and views, while executing model queries, validation checks, and trade studies to inform engineering and sustainment decisions; link model elements to PLM-managed configuration items to maintain digital thread traceability.

  • Identify and manage obsolescence and Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) risks, supporting proactive technology refresh and parts management strategies.

  • Coordinate with cloud, cybersecurity, data, and application development teams to support scalable, secure enterprise PLM and digital engineering solutions.

  • Participate in governance boards, configuration control boards, technical reviews, stakeholder meetings, and program status briefings.

  • Support development of technical roadmaps, PLM/digital thread implementation strategies, and data migration plans.

  • Monitor project risks, dependencies, technical issues, and integration impacts across sustainment and modernization initiatives.

  • Contribute to continuous improvement efforts, digital engineering standards development, and operational readiness planning.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related discipline and 8–10 years of related experience, or 6–10 years with a Master’s degree. Additional experience may be considered in lieu of degree.

  • Demonstrated experience in sustainment engineering or product support engineering for complex systems, including lifecycle support planning, configuration management, and readiness analysis.

  • Hands-on experience with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software such as PTC Windchill or Siemens Teamcenter, including product structure/BOM management, change management workflows, and document/data management.

  • Experience with digital thread management: establishing and maintaining authoritative, traceable linkages between requirements, models, design data, configuration baselines, and sustainment data across the system lifecycle.

  • Experience supporting complex federal IT, systems engineering, or modernization programs.

  • Familiarity with systems engineering lifecycle processes and requirements management practices.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • U.S. Citizenship required.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DHS Public Trust and Secret clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading or supporting an enterprise-scale deployment of a PLM environment (e.g., Windchill or Teamcenter), including architecture definition, data migration, workflow configuration, integration with ERP/MBSE/logistics tools, and user adoption/training.

  • OMG Certified Systems Modeling Professional (OCSMP) – Model Builder certification, or equivalent demonstrated MBSE proficiency (SysML/UAFML, Cameo Enterprise Architecture).

  • Experience integrating MBSE environments (e.g., Cameo/Teamwork Cloud) with PLM platforms to maintain a continuous digital thread between architecture models and configuration-managed product data.

  • Familiarity with logistics product data and integrated product support standards (e.g., GEIA-STD-0007, S1000D, MIL-STD-3046, ANSI/EIA-649 configuration management principles).

  • Experience with DMSMS/obsolescence management programs and sustainment cost or level-of-repair analyses.

  • Experience supporting U.S. Coast Guard, DHS, or DoD sustainment, logistics, or product data management programs.

title: Senior Group Product Manager
description:
Ready for a challenge?

Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.

Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.

About this role:

The Discovery Experience is the front door to JET's product - the first thing millions of customers see every time they open the app. Getting it right matters enormously, both for the customer experience and for the commercial performance of the business, and this is the team that owns it.

As Senior Group PM for Discovery Experience, you’ll lead a team of PMs across a remit that spans the full Discovery Experience that work with algorithms and AI that power personalisation, to the experiments that prove what actually works, to the longer-term strategic bets that will define how this surface evolves at JET. This is a role with real breadth and genuine complexity. The Discovery Experience sits at the intersection of customer needs, restaurant priorities, and commercial goals - and those don't always point in the same direction. You'll need to make clear, well-reasoned calls about where to focus and bring a range of senior stakeholders with you. On the experimentation side, there's a significant opportunity to raise the bar - the foundations are there, but JET is on a journey to make testing faster, more rigorous, and more deeply embedded in how product decisions get made.

These are some of the key components to the position:

  • Homepage strategy - You will own and guide the product strategy for the Discovery experience, our highest-traffic and most commercially important surface

  • Full product ownership - Drive the end-to-end product lifecycle, from discovery and prioritisation through to delivery and iteration, balancing short-term performance with long-term vision

  • Experimentation - Set the standard for how we run tests in the Discovery experience, using experimentation as a core tool to validate decisions and drive measurable impact

  • Personalisation - This is one of the biggest levers available to the Discovery Experience, and you'll work closely with data science and engineering to shape the models and ranking logic that serve the right experience to the customer at the right moment

  • AI and algorithmic product development - Work closely with data science and engineering to shape the algorithms and AI-powered features that personalise and optimise the Homepage experience at scale

  • Team leadership - Manage and coach a team of product managers, helping them grow into strong, autonomous PMs

  • Stakeholder influence - Work closely with engineering, design, data science, and senior leadership to align on priorities and shape the direction of the Discovery Experience

  • Cross-functional collaboration - Partner across the business to ensure the experience reflects the needs of customers, partners, and commercial goals alike

What will you bring to the team?

  • Product craft - A strong track record of owning and shipping impactful product, with the instincts to know what to build, when, and why

  • Experimentation expertise - Deep experience running rigorous A/B tests and the statistical literacy to design, evaluate, and act on results with confidence

  • AI and algorithmic fluency - Experience working on products powered by recommendation engines, ranking algorithms, or machine learning models, and the ability to collaborate effectively with data science teams to drive better customer outcomes

  • Leadership and coaching - Experience managing a team of PMs, with a genuine commitment to developing people and raising the bar

  • Strategic thinking - The ability to zoom out, connect the dots across customer, commercial, and business goals, and turn ambiguity into a clear direction

  • Data fluency - You're comfortable getting into the data yourself, asking the right questions, and building arguments grounded in evidence

  • Influence without authority - You bring people with you through clear thinking, strong communication, and well-reasoned conviction

  • Curiosity about customers - A genuine desire to understand consumer behaviour and use those insights to build a Homepage that works harder for every user

At JET, this is how we play

Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment. Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.

At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.

Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.

Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging

No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.

What else is cooking?

Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET morsels.

Are you ready to take your seat? Apply now!

title: Senior Cyber Defense Analyst
description:
Leidos' Corporate Information Security Office, reporting through the Digital sector, is seeking a Senior Cyber Defense Analyst.

This is an opportunity to join a team of highly skilled and innovative network defenders, and the best group of individuals out there. Leidos' Cybersecurity Intelligence and Response Team (CSIRT) has an immediate opening for a motivated Cyber Defense Analyst. Leidos is an international company made up of 50,000 employees that provides Defense, Intelligence and Health Products to our customers. Our goal is to stay ahead of, and maintain a technical advantage over our adversaries.

As a key part of the team, your responsibilities will include threat hunting, and tactical analysis of ongoing attacks by criminal and nation state actors. You will perform data analysis, incident response, investigative analysis, and research on existing and emerging cyber threats, particularly those directed against Leidos' global networks. You will be expected to "think like an adversary" and engage in threat hunting operations leveraging your understanding of the tactics, techniques and procedures employed by advanced threats combined with intelligence from multiple sources, and provide reporting and briefings to other teams and leadership in order to maintain appropriate levels of situational awareness.

A CSIRT That's Evolving Through Hyperautomation and Agentic AI

Our CSIRT is actively maturing its operations by integrating hyperautomation and agentic AI into the detection, triage, and response lifecycle. Rather than relying solely on manual playbooks, the team is building and deploying intelligent automation that can orchestrate routine investigative steps, correlate signals across disparate tools, and accelerate the path from alert to action. This is a chance to help define what a modern, AI-augmented CSIRT looks like — combining seasoned analyst tradecraft with cutting-edge automation to outpace adversaries at scale.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Analyze network and host activity associated with both successful and unsuccessful intrusions by advanced attackers.

  • Perform network traffic analysis utilizing raw packet data, net flow, IDS, and custom sensor output.

  • Support enterprise incident response efforts.

  • Leverage understanding of tactics, techniques and procedures associated with advanced threats to create and add custom signatures that mitigate highly dynamic threats to the enterprise.

  • Employ advanced forensic tools and techniques for attack reconstruction and intelligence gathering.

  • Proactively research emerging cyber threats. Apply analytical understanding of attacker methodologies and tactics, system vulnerabilities, and key indicators of attacks and exploits.

  • Contribute to threat intelligence reports and briefings that provide situational awareness of cyber threats impacting the company's global network infrastructure, to every level of the organization.

  • Participate in threat hunt operations using known adversary tactics, techniques and procedures, as well as indicators of attack, in order to detect advanced threats to the enterprise.

  • Collaborate using information and knowledge sharing networks and professional relationships to achieve common goals.

  • Provide on-call support for incident response efforts outside of core hours, as needed.

  • Mentor junior analysts technically and conceptually

  • Lead small groups within the team for discernable tasks, including projects and incident response

  • Drive advanced countermeasures through to completion

  • Understanding and educating the team about defending new threat vectors

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Must be a U.S. Citizen and eligible to obtain DoD Secret clearance.

  • BS Degree and 8-12 years relevant experience in cyber security or network defense; or equivalent education and years of relevant experience coupled with relevant certifications (CISSP, SANS GIAC, CEH, etc.) may be considered in lieu of degree..

  • Experience in conventional network\host-based intrusion analysis, digital forensics, or malware analysis.

  • Experience performing "deep dive" analysis and correlation of log data from multiple sources including PCAP and forensic artifacts.

  • Experience leading and contributing to incident response activities

  • Strong understanding of Operating Systems and Network Protocols.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Windows administrative tools, and the Unix/Linux command line.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Understanding of behavioral based threat models, including ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain, Diamond Model, etc.

  • Experience with Splunk (preferred) or other SIEM-type platform

  • Capable and comfortable communicating actionable threat intelligence to both technical and executive-level stakeholders.

  • Familiarity with common languages (like Perl and Python) to parse logs, automate processes, and integrate systems.

  • Previous experience as Threat Researcher and/or Intelligence Analyst.

  • Experience with dynamic malware analysis, and reverse engineering.

  • Experience in cryptography or cryptanalysis

  • Experience in cyber security engineering

  • Experience defending large cloud infrastructures (AWS, Azure, etc.)

  • Ability to create, modify, and implement both Snort and YARA signatures.

  • Published research papers at conferences or through other mediums (blogs, articles).

  • Working knowledge of Computer Network Exploitation (CNE), Computer Network Attack (CNA) and Computer Network Defense (CND) tools and techniques.

  • A deep understanding of advanced cyber threats targeting enterprises, along with the tools, tactics, and procedures used by those threats.

  • Experience applying threat and data modeling, advanced data correlation, and statistical analysis to develop alerts, notable events, investigative dashboards, and metrics driven reports.

As Product Owner for Payments, you will own the backlog and product vision for a payment delivery team within our broader payment area, which covers everything from card and digital wallet processing to open banking, alternative payment methods, cashier experience, wallet management, transaction history, and the compliance and AML obligations that surround all of it.

You will join a payment product group that already has strong UX, data and delivery expertise. What you bring is the financial and payment industry grounding that turns infrastructure investment into commercial outcomes, along with the product craft to make complex, regulated systems feel simple for our customers.

The Role

Payments is one of the most strategically critical domains in our business. Every euro that moves, whether deposited, withdrawn, or held in a wallet, passes through systems you will own the product direction for.

As Product Owner for Payments, you will own the backlog and product vision for a payment delivery team within our broader payment area, which covers everything from card and digital wallet processing to open banking, alternative payment methods, cashier experience, wallet management, transaction history, and the compliance and AML obligations that surround all of it.

You will join a payment product group that already has strong UX, data and delivery expertise. What you bring is the financial and payment industry grounding that turns infrastructure investment into commercial outcomes, along with the product craft to make complex, regulated systems feel simple for our customers.

What You Will Do

Product Direction and Backlog

  • translate business needs, regulatory requirements, and market opportunities into clear Epics and User Stories with meaningful acceptance criteria
  • Make tough prioritisation calls across feature delivery, compliance obligations, technical health, and new market or brand launches, and be able to articulate the trade-offs clearly to your stakeholders
  • Assess what has been delivered, review outcomes against expectations, and continuously refine the next slice of work.

Working With Your Team

  • Work in close partnership with the Technical Engineering Manager (TEM), who is responsible for how the team works, including ways of working, capacity management, and the conditions for delivery. You are accountable for what gets built and why; together you give the team everything it needs to move with confidence.
  • Actively participate in team ceremonies, clarify requirements, accept delivered work, and ensure what ships matches what was intended.
  • Stay connected to the team's health and pace and adjust scope accordingly.

Stakeholder Management and Alignment

  • Act as the primary product voice for your team, responsible for defining what gets built next and why, with the authority and accountability to match.
  • Engage stakeholders across Finance, Compliance, Risk, Operations, and Engineering; manage expectations and communicate progress with transparency.
  • Partner with the Product Engineering Lead to shape the broader payment roadmap, and communicate the longer-term direction so that planning conversations are informed and grounded.
  • Represent your domain in cross-team initiatives spanning multiple payment teams, compliance programmes, or brand launches.

Metrics-Driven Decision Making

  • Define and track meaningful KPIs for your product area: deposit and withdrawal success rates, cashier conversion, payment method performance, and provider reliability.
  • Use data, analytics, and customer feedback to validate that features deliver intended value and change course quickly when they don't.
  • Protect long-term product and system health alongside feature throughput. In a regulated payment system, technical health and product health are the same thing.

Customer and Market Understanding

  • Bring a genuine understanding of the payment journey from the customer's perspective, from selecting a payment method in the cashier to a withdrawal landing in their bank account.
  • Stay informed about developments in payment regulation, scheme rules, and customer expectations across our markets so the roadmap is never caught off guard.
  • Work closely with our UX function to ensure the cashier experience across web, mobile web, and native apps is best-in-class for our customers.

How We Work

Our payment teams are cross-functional: backend, frontend, and native developers, testers, and the Product Owner work together in a single team. Everyone is expected to contribute across the team's needs, not just their own specialism.

We work in short cycles, release frequently, and learn from what we ship. The teams own their own releases, monitor their own systems, and manage their own incidents. If something goes wrong in production, the team responds together and the PO is part of understanding what happened and what to do next.

Your Experience:

Essential

  • Experience in a regulated financial services or gaming environment. You understand what it means to build products where compliance is non-negotiable and where mistakes have real consequences for customers and the business.
  • Minimum 3 years as a Product Owner in a cross-functional agile team, with a proven ability to manage a complex, multi-dependency backlog under real pressure.
  • Strong track record of translating regulatory or compliance requirements into clear, actionable product work without losing sight of the customer experience.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. You can present a prioritisation trade-off to a Finance director in the morning and write acceptance criteria with your engineering team in the afternoon.
  • Data and evidence drive your decisions. You are comfortable defining KPIs, reading dashboards, and changing your mind when the data says you were wrong.
  • A genuine understanding of iterative delivery, not just the ceremonies but the thinking behind them. You know the difference between a team that is busy and a team that is producing value.

Domain Knowledge - Valued, Not Required

We know that strong payment product owners are rare. Domain knowledge is valuable and we will actively look for it, but we will not filter out strong candidates who lack it. Product craft, commercial sharpness, and the ability to learn a complex domain quickly matter more.

Any of the following will help you get up to speed faster:

  • Background from a payment service provider, acquirer, card scheme, or merchant payments team.
  • Familiarity with how card payments, digital wallets, or open banking work end-to-end, well enough to ask the right questions and spot the risks.
  • Experience with payment regulation or compliance-adjacent product work (PSD2, AML, KYC, responsible gambling).
  • Experience owning customer-facing transactional journeys such as cashiers, checkout flows, or onboarding with payment components.
  • Experience working across multiple markets, brands, or jurisdictions simultaneously.

We believe talent knows no boundaries. Our hiring process focuses solely on your skills, experience, and potential to contribute to our team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and evaluate each candidate based on merit, regardless of personal characteristics as the age, gender, origin, religion, sexual orientation, neurodiversity or disability.

JOB SUMMARY & RESPONSIBILITIES

The Plant Technician Intern will learn the operation of plant processing equipment and perform routine basic maintenance in a highly automated chemical facility. In the area of maintenance, Plant Technician Interns will learn the safe and efficient maintenance, basic repair, and cleaning of equipment associated with bioprocessing processes. At times, Plant Technician Interns may be asked to assist Maintenance Technicians in more technical and complex maintenance procedures. Team members in this position will gain knowledge of the process flow, computerized equipment, and be aware of hazards associated with the process as well as learn, understand, and execute standard operating procedures (SOPs). Continuous plant operation may require 12-hour shift work. The Plant Technician Intern must be able to adapt to 12-hour workdays and be able to meet call-in requirements if needed.

This is an on-site role located in North Manchester, IN. Responsibilities include:

  • Use your knowledge to maintain and operate all processes associated with the plant where required.

  • Perform maintenance and basic repairs of plant equipment and document these activities.

  • Operate the DCS (Distributed Control System) for the plant.

  • Safely perform basic electrical troubleshooting.

  • Follow procedures for plant start-up, shut-down, cleaning, and batching.

  • Maintain accurate and timely logs.

  • Collect and test quality control samples, interpret QA/QC results and make adjustments to optimize plant operations, timely and accurately document results and enter results into our data collection system, PI.

  • Assist in removal, installation, rebuild, and performance of preventive and predictive maintenance on all equipment associated with plant processes.

  • Help to keep your plant clean by following the sanitation schedule and completing all tasks as assigned.

  • Notify the management team of safety, environmental, quality and production concerns, problems and opportunities.

  • Keep your plant safe by fostering a culture of safe behavior and environmental compliance.

  • Maintain a team environment at all times and champion POET in the community.

  • Foster a culture of safe behavior and environmental compliance at all times.

  • Maintain and advance the food safety and quality of POET’s products and processes to deliver a best-in-class culture of quality.

  • Since we’re all about teamwork and getting the job done, your skills may be put to a lot of other uses!

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Currently attending accredited learning institution related to bio-processing, energy production, or plant maintenance.

  • Working knowledge in math, reading comprehension and mechanical reasoning required.

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills are required.

  • Experience with software systems, such as Maximo, preferred.

  • Excellent organizational, time management, and communication skills as well as the ability to embrace change.

  • You know the basics of Microsoft Office Suite. You’re capable of learning new programs.

A SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE

  • High level of personal integrity

  • Interpersonal skills – ability to effectively interact with individuals at all levels within/outside the organization

  • Ability to embrace and promote change

  • Innovative mindset

  • Ability to think objectively

  • Self-awareness in the face of uncertainty

  • Ability to work in a team environment

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

This role has some physical requirements that our team members will need to be able to perform, such as:

  • Wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as hard hats, gloves, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, hazardous material suit, hearing protection, and harness.

  • Working at extreme heights (approximately 150 ft), in confined spaces, and in extreme temperatures from -20 to +100 degrees Fahrenheit, both indoors and outdoors. Due to the nature of the work, the areas can be dusty at times.

  • Must be able to use the following equipment/tools, with training provided (not all encompassing): forklift, power washer, pallet jack, hoist systems, scissor lifts, JLG lifts, telehandlers, Front End Loaders, various hand tools, and computers.

Frequently:

  • Sitting in a chair in the Control Room while operating the plant

  • Walk indoors and outdoors, sometimes over rough, uneven, or wet/slick surfaces

  • Carry to up to 15lbs

  • Climb stairs and/or ladders

  • Stand indoors to clean and maintain areas

  • Reach at arm’s length to gather samples

  • Be in awkward back, shoulder, wrist, and hand positions

  • Use coordination and grip, with a force of up to 50lbs

  • Bend while standing

  • Use repetitive arm motions to wipe down and maintain work area

  • Climb in and out of Powered Industrial Vehicles

Occasionally:

  • Lift up to 50lbs, with or without assistance

  • Carry up to 40 lbs, with our without assistance

  • Push with a force of 10lbs, with or without assistance

  • Pull with a force of up to 85lbs, with or without assistance

  • Bend, twist, turn, kneel, and crouch, while holding light and medium-weighted objects

Since we are all about teamwork, you may be asked to help other roles that have their own unique set of physical requirements.

Due to the physical and safety-sensitive nature of this job, you will be subject to a physical and expected to pass a drug screen during the pre-screen process. During employment, you’ll be subject to random drug and alcohol testing.

CULTURE IS KING AT POET

We’re all on the same team. We always communicate. And we park our egos at the door. These aren’t just slogans on our walls. It’s the way we do things at POET. We provide an environment for team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance. It’s the best way to optimize health, wellness, and productivity in a sustainable way. We work hard. We play hard. We have frequent team events, volunteer efforts, and we know how to celebrate wins!

GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES

At POET we encourage internal development and growth by allowing team members to carve their own path to success. Leaders support team members with the necessary resources to develop their skills, achieve goals, and create the most value. We believe in developing our team members to their highest potential and recognizing contributions that add value to the organization. Each new team member’s position and compensation are carefully determined by considering their unique qualifications and skillset.

Job Description

Position Summary

Vassar College is seeking a full-time, entry- level Study Abroad Advisor, reporting to the Associate Director in the Office of International Programs (OIP). Joining an experienced, creative and inclusive team, the Study Abroad Advisor collaborates with on-campus and off-campus stakeholders to administer the education abroad application and enrollment processes, support students during all phases of study abroad, and promote the College’s commitment to access, inclusion and belonging. The Advisor will support the College’s global engagement, a key aspect of Vassar’s liberal arts education. The core function of OIP is to steward student participation in education abroad.

Nearly 50% of Vassar students study abroad for a full semester or an academic year prior to graduation; additional students participate in short-term programs associated with on-campus classes or special programs. The OIP partners with faculty to administer Vassar-only programs in London and Clifden, and consortial programs in Berlin, Bologna, Paris, and Madrid. OIP also manages Vassar's exchange partnerships with institutions in Paris, Beijing, Tokyo, Exeter, Toulouse, and Singapore. In addition to Vassar programs, the office manages a list of approximately 130 other approved programs that students may access. OIP also supports a number of other global partnerships and initiatives.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide in-depth study abroad advising to students with an understanding of Vassar

degree plans and Vassar’s student learning goals for study abroad participants.

  • Learn and maintain detailed knowledge of the Office of International Programs' portfolio of study abroad programs and partnerships, specifically Vassar-approved programs.

  • Lead advising on study abroad scholarships.

  • Regularly lead programming, spanning from study abroad promotion to re-entry.

  • Support the Associate Director with application management.

  • Assist the Associate Director with general and program-specific communications to students; manage e-newsletters for students in the pre-departure and while abroad phases.

  • Assist the Associate Director with the program evaluation collection and analysis process.

  • Maintain relationships with institutional and program provider representatives for effective day to day communications related to application, enrollment, and advising processes.

  • Participate in international education conferences and program site-visits as necessary.

  • Regularly engage in the field of international education to stay up to date on innovative study abroad engagement and advising practices.

Required knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

  • Intercultural training, cross cultural experience, and/or experience living abroad

  • Demonstrated motivation to enhance inclusion in education abroad or other settings

  • Ability to advise students from diverse backgrounds on experiences of transition, adjustment, and navigation of a new environment

  • Ability to work proactively and independently, while also collaboratively as part of a team while managing a wide variety of tasks and priorities

  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills

  • Strong attention to detail, organizational, and problem-solving skills

  • Capacity to manage a high volume of detailed information with frequent interruptions

  • Demonstrated ability to diplomatically communicate and collaborate with diverse stakeholders

  • Proficiency in Google suite

  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally to participate in conferences and conduct program site visits.

  • Ability to periodically flex hours for evening or weekend programming.

  • Ability to interact effectively with a diverse community.

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time.

Preferred knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • Experience working in higher education, international education, or a related field.

  • Experience with Canva, social media platforms, and familiarity with study abroad data and application management systems (such as Terra Dotta)

Compensation

The compensation for this position is $62,353.20 - $70,000 per year.

When extending an offer, Vassar College considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, budget, and other market and organizational considerations. The starting salary range represents the College’s good faith and reasonable estimate at the time of posting.

To complete your application, you will be required to attach your resume and cover letter.

If you are excited about this role but you feel unsure that your experience aligns perfectly, please still consider applying. We encourage you to think broadly about your background and skills as you may have experience outside of the requirements that add value to your candidacy.

Focused on meeting Discovery & Medical customer expectations for quality, cost and delivery, the role drives Associate engagement, labor and overhead productivity, and effective deployment of people and reliable equipment.   • Partner with site-based EHS & Facilities, Supply Chain, Quality, and DBS leaders to identify critical performance gaps, lead Kaizen events, and execute breakthrough initiatives that improve customer value and operational performance.

  • Lead Manufacturing Engineering and Reliability Engineering teams to optimize process capability, equipment performance, technology deployment, validation readiness and lifecycle asset reliability across all manufacturing platforms.

  • Build strong cross-functional relationships with upstream suppliers, downstream supply chain partners and internal stakeholders to improve flow, reduce disruption, and increase responsiveness across the full value stream.

  • Develop, coach and engage manufacturing and engineering talent, strengthening leadership capability, DBS competency, associate engagement and succession depth across the site.

Who you are:

  • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in relevant Business, Manufacturing, Engineering or Science based discipline, or equivalent years of experience.

  • Significant progressive experience in complex site manufacturing and engineering leadership within a high-volume, lean-driven manufacturing environment, ideally in Life Sciences or a similar regulated industry with high levels of automation.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex problems, communicate issues, and propose solutions to external customers and internal team members.

  • Strong analytical, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate ideas clearly, build understanding, and strengthen problem solving and relationships across peers and leaders.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a multi-tasking, dynamic environment, while maintaining a forward-thinking and customer-first attitude.

  • Ability to energize, develop, build rapport, collaborate, and influence at all levels within an organization. Acts as an inspirational, approachable, and humble leader who builds trust and engagement.

Travel, Motor Vehicle Record & Physical/Environment Requirements:

  • Ability to travel up to 20% of the time, including visits to manufacturing sites and business locations as required.

  • Ability to work in a variety of manufacturing, cleanroom, laboratory, biological production, and office environments.

It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:

title: Computer Analyst– Sankaran Lab
description:
Primary Work Address: 300 Longwood Avenue, Boston, MA, 02115

Current HHMI Employees, click here to apply via your Workday account.

We have an outstanding opportunity for a Computer Analyst to join the Sankaran lab at Boston Children's Hospital. The Sankaran Laboratory uses human genetics to study hematopoiesis and how this process goes awry in human disease. We are particularly interested in gaining molecular insights into how hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells can effectively produce mature blood and immune cells. We integrate modern human genetic studies with functional studies, employing a variety of innovative genomic technologies and more traditional hematopoietic assays. Additionally, we develop genomic tools, including cellular barcoding approaches and single-cell technologies, to enable higher-resolution studies of human hematopoiesis in health and disease. More information about the lab and their work can be found by visiting:

About the role:
Join our lab to help drive forward our quantitative and computational research. In this role, you'll work closely with our computational lead and fellow scientists, playing a key part in expanding the lab's capacity and speed in tackling computational challenges.

We're looking for someone who thrives on taking ownership of well-defined, modular projects, someone who writes clean, well-documented, reproducible code and brings a critical eye to interpreting results within their research context. As you grow in the role, you'll gain increasing independence, while knowing when to loop in the computational lead or PI on trickier problems.

This position is a great fit if you enjoy:

  • Building reproducible computational pipelines

  • Picking up new tools and technologies with curiosity

  • Collaborating across a variety of research projects

What we provide:

  • Opportunity to work with a dynamic, diverse, and highly collaborative research team seeking to define how blood diseases arise and how better treatments can be developed.

  • Access to several vibrant research communities in the Boston area, including at Boston Children's Hospital, the broader Longwood medical area centered around Harvard Medical School, and the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard.

  • Close interactions with colleagues and collaborators in human genetics and computational biology.

  • A competitive compensation package with comprehensive health and welfare benefits.

What you’ll do:

  • Execute and monitor computational workflows (HPC/Cloud) using established tools and pipelines under the guidance of the computational lead.

  • Generate research outputs (tables, figures, summary statistics) and communicate progress, findings, and issues to the team in a timely manner.

  • Assist lab members with troubleshooting and routine tasks. Perform quality checks, troubleshoot routine computational errors, and escalate non-routine problems to the computational lead with relevant logs, diagnostics, and observations.

  • Develop, document, and improve computational workflows, automation scripts, and reproducible research practices.

  • Depending on experience and interests, the position may provide opportunities to develop increasingly independent computational analyses and contribute to research publications.

  • The candidate should be comfortable asking questions when requirements are unclear, documenting their work, and communicating unexpected results rather than simply producing an output without verification.

  • You will meet regularly with the computational lead, as well as the lab PI (at least biweekly) to review ongoing work and strategize.

What you bring:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer-related field; or an equivalent combination of education and related work experience.

  • Demonstrated programming or scripting experience in Python, R, and/or Bash.

  • Experience with Linux/Unix environments, command-line tools, and collaborating through Git version control.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies or unexpected results in computational analyses.

  • Ability to learn unfamiliar computational tools and workflows independently.

  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize tasks in consultation with the computational lead, communicate progress, and meet agreed-upon deadlines.

  • Experience working with large datasets or computational workloads on HPC or cloud platforms is a plus.

  • Experience with workflow-management systems such as Nextflow is a plus.

  • Experience with data visualization and statistical analysis.

  • Demonstrated experience with reproducible computational research practices is a plus.

Physical Requirements

Remaining in a normal seated or standing position for extended periods of time; reaching and grasping by extending hand(s) or arm(s); dexterity to manipulate objects with fingers, for example using a keyboard; communication skills using the spoken word; ability to see and hear within normal parameters; ability to move about workspace. The position requires mobility, including the ability to move materials weighing up to several pounds (such as a laptop computer or tablet).

Persons with disabilities may be able to perform the essential duties of this position with reasonable accommodation. Requests for reasonable accommodation will be evaluated on an individual basis.

This job description sets forth the job’s principal duties, responsibilities, and requirements; it should not be construed as an exhaustive statement, however. Unless they begin with the word “may,” the Essential Duties and Responsibilities described above are “essential functions” of the job, as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act.

title: CPU Verification Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here! At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. Dynamic, hard-working people and inspiring, innovative technologies are the norm here. The people who work here have reinvented entire industries with all Apple Hardware products. The same passion for innovation that goes into our products also applies to our practices strengthening our commitment to leave the world better than we found it! Join us to help deliver the next groundbreaking Apple product. In this highly visible role, you will be at the center of a chip design effort collaborating with all disciplines, with a critical impact on getting functional products to millions of customers quickly.

As a CPU Verification Engineer owning the verification of a certain area of functionality in a CPU design, you will have the responsibilities as follows: - Work closely with architecture and RTL designers on verifying the functionality correctness of the design - Develop and lead test plan and test environments - Develop complex tests in assembly, C, or vectors according to test plans - Develop coverage monitors and analyze coverage to ensure all the test cases in the plans are covered - Develop checkers or C-base transactor to verify the design

Minimum Qualifications

    • BS EE/CE or equivalent experience.
    • Be an outstanding teammate with excellent communication skills and the desire to address diverse challenges.

Preferred Qualifications

    • We're looking for someone who is well-rounded in all aspects of verification.
    • Knowledge of CPU & SOC architecture/design & in-depth knowledge of verification flow.
    • Thrive by demonstrating your expertise with low-level programming of sophisticated computer systems in C/C++/assembly.
    • Being already familiar verification environments such as UVM and System Verilog will come a long way with us.
    • Apply knowledge of industry standard interfaces and have a deep understanding of Verilog, Verilog simulator, and debuggers.
    • Have a detailed understanding of the constrained random verification process, functional coverage, code coverage, assertion methodology & philosophy.
    • Even better if you also have knowledge of formal, hardware acceleration.

title: Director Quality Control
description:
Working with Us
Challenging. Meaningful. Life-changing. Those aren’t words that are usually associated with a job. But working at Bristol Myers Squibb is anything but usual. Here, uniquely interesting work happens every day, in every department. From optimizing a production line to the latest breakthroughs in cell therapy, this is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. You’ll get the chance to grow and thrive through opportunities uncommon in scale and scope, alongside high-achieving teams. Take your career farther than you thought possible.

Bristol Myers Squibb recognizes the importance of balance and flexibility in our work environment. We offer a wide variety of competitive benefits, services and programs that provide our employees with the resources to pursue their goals, both at work and in their personal lives. Read more: .

Position Summary

The Director Quality Control (QC) is responsible for leading all Quality Control laboratory operations, ensuring the timely delivery of testing activities, including drug product, intermediates, stability, raw materials, and microbiology/environmental monitoring. This role ensures that all testing is executed in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, cGMP standards, company policies, and local procedures.

As a key quality leader, the Director QC oversees multiple laboratory teams with diverse functions, providing strategic direction, resource planning, performance management, and goal setting to drive operational excellence and continuous improvement. The role is accountable for ensuring the timely closure of laboratory investigations and associated CAPAs, while maintaining a strong culture of quality, compliance, and inspection readiness.

The Director QC also has full ownership of the Quality Control budget, ensuring effective financial stewardship, resource allocation, and investment decisions that support business objectives and future growth. Through strong leadership and cross-functional collaboration, this role plays a pivotal part in delivering safe, effective, and high-quality products to patients.

Duties/Responsibilities

  • Directs QC laboratory to ensure timely completion of testing (e.g., drug product, intermediates, stability, raw materials) that is performed in compliance with regulatory agencies, cGMP, and other company policies and procedures.
  • Defines departmental roles and accountabilities. Hires, integrates, and develops high-quality talent capable of delivering against the department’s goals and objectives.
  • Establishes and communicates performance objectives for QC staff that are consistent with the business unit and Quality goals. Defines and monitors performance measures, provides developmental feedback and coaching, and creates a collaborative environment that attracts, develops, and retains the best talent.
  • Accountable for lifecycle management of analytical methods and technology within the QC laboratory.
  • Directs and participates in continuous improvement efforts to drive business efficiencies (e.g., TAT improvements, COGM reductions).
  • Directs programs which assure the proper operation and maintenance of laboratory equipment and the timely data analysis and reporting of trends.
  • Participates in the site team, which prepares for, hosts, and responds to regulatory inspections, reviews, and approvals of the facility and products.
  • Accountable for on time completion of quality records within the QMS.
  • Accountable for completion of Annual Product Quality Review and periodic investigation trending reports.
  • Verifies compliance with applicable BMS Policies and Procedures and ensures consistency with other site procedures and/or specifications.
  • Responsible for managing the QC Operations budget.
  • Fosters collaboration and communication across site and network teams. Collaborates with managers across the QC network to harmonize best practices.
  • Performs other tasks as required to support the QC laboratories.

Qualifications

Specific Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • Ability to work independently and to collaborate cross functionally and at network level to drive operational and quality excellence.
  • Advanced leadership, strategic thinking, critical reasoning, troubleshooting, and decision-making skills to resolve complex scenarios.
  • Advanced mentoring and coaching, influencing, negotiating, and personal interaction skills.
  • Advanced knowledge of regulations and guidelines as related to the manufacture of cell therapy products e.g.: cGMP, ISO, FDA, MHRA, USP, and EP.
  • Experience with method validation and technical transfer.
  • In depth knowledge of QMS and its application to the QC laboratory
  • Advanced verbal and written communication skills with the ability to tailor style for a wide variety of audiences.
  • Experience leading forecasting, capacity modeling, and resource planning.

Education/Experience/ Licenses/Certifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Chemistry, Cell Biology, or related science. Advanced degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 12 years of relevant work experience required
  • Minimum 6 years of increasing management responsibility of a cell therapy, drug product, or related biopharmaceutical Quality Control laboratory.

title: Order to Cash Specialist - Americas and Export
description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

The Order to Cash Specialist is responsible for executing the day-to-day Order to Cash activities for dealer, distributor, and export customers across the Americas and Export markets. This role supports order processing, customer support, invoicing, credits, returns, and shipment coordination while ensuring accurate and timely execution of orders from order entry through invoicing.

The specialist works closely with Sales, Logistics, Distribution, Finance, and the Order to Cash Supervisor to ensure orders are processed accurately, customers are supported proactively, and shipments and invoicing are completed on time.

This role plays an important part in delivering a high level of customer service and operational execution consistent with a premium or luxury brand experience.

Key Responsibilities

Order Management & Execution

  • Enter and manage sales orders for dealer, distributor, demo, marketing, endorsement, trade show, and export customers
  • Ensure orders are entered accurately, released appropriately, and shipped on time
  • Monitor open orders and backlog and help resolve order holds, stock issues, and credit blocks
  • Coordinate with Logistics and Distribution on shipment scheduling and delivery status
  • Provide shipment tracking, order status updates, and proactive communication to customers and Sales teams
  • Maintain order status reports and backlog tracking tools

Customer & Commercial Support

  • Support Sales teams with order status, inventory availability, and shipment timing
  • Respond to dealer, distributor, and customer inquiries related to orders, shipments, invoicing, and returns
  • Support new customer onboarding and order flow setup
  • Assist with dealer and distributor program execution, including credits, rebates, co-op, MDF, and returns coordination
  • Maintain customer master data and account records in ERP systems

Inventory, Backlog & Supply Chain Coordination

  • Work with Demand Planning and Supply Planning teams to monitor inventory availability and expected ship dates
  • Provide visibility to Sales teams on inventory and order status
  • Support backlog management and order prioritization during constrained supply situations
  • Maintain reports related to inventory availability, order status, and demo allocations

Credit, Invoicing & Cash Flow Support

  • Ensure invoices are generated accurately and on time
  • Process credit and rebill transactions and support pricing adjustments and corrections
  • Process dealer and distributor credits after validating required documentation
  • Support Accounts Receivable with dispute resolution and deduction research
  • Help manage credit blocks and support cash collection follow-up where needed

Returns, Export & Documentation

  • Process return authorizations and coordinate return shipments
  • Prepare commercial invoices and export documentation for international shipments
  • Ensure export documentation is complete and accurate
  • Coordinate returns related to dealers, engineering, and marketing/demo equipment

Process & Reporting Support

  • Maintain order, shipment, backlog, and credit tracking reports
  • Support process improvement initiatives and system improvements
  • Follow standard operating procedures and support documentation updates
  • Escalate recurring issues related to orders, invoicing, shipping, or credits

Key Performance Metrics

  • Order entry accuracy
  • On Time In Full (OTIF) shipment performance
  • Backlog aging
  • Invoice accuracy
  • Credit processing cycle time
  • Customer response and resolution time
  • Order processing turnaround time

Skills & Experience

  • Experience in Order Management, Customer Service, Sales Administration, or Order to Cash operations
  • Experience supporting dealer, distributor, export, or B2B customers preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • ERP system experience (JDE, SAP, etc.)
  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • Ability to work across Sales, Logistics, Finance, and Supply Chain teams
  • Problem solving and follow-through skills
  • Experience with export documentation a plus

* Monitor environmental conditions within the van (temperature, ventilation) to ensure optimal conditions for chick transport.
* Maintain accurate records of mileage, fuel consumption, and delivery details.
* Communicate effectively with dispatch, farm staff, and other relevant personnel.
* Adhere to strict biosecurity protocols to prevent the spread of diseases.
* Perform routine cleaning and sanitization of the vehicle.
* Respond to emergencies or unexpected situations during transportation.

Job Qualifications**

* Valid Heavy Commercial (HC) or Pink Light Commercial (PNKLN LADA) driver's license with a clean driving record.
* Minimum 2 years of experience in commercial driving, preferably with livestock or fragile goods.
* Knowledge of vehicle maintenance and basic troubleshooting.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
* Strong commitment to animal welfare and safety.
* Good communication and interpersonal skills.
* Physically fit and able to lift and move heavy objects (chick crates).
* Willingness to work flexible hours, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends as required.
* Understanding of biosecurity principles is a plus.

FCM takes a holistic approach to corporate travel, specializing in managing national and global travel programs for medium and large businesses.

To learn more about FCM please click HERE

FCM is seeking a strategic and commercially minded Head of Global Account Management to lead and evolve our global account management function.   • Giving Back: Our Corporate Social Responsibility program supports nominated charities through volunteering and fundraising, complemented by our Office Environmental Program, LEED® Gold-certified office spaces, and 1 paid Volunteer Day per calendar year.

description:

This is an exciting opportunity to join one of our high-performing branches, designed to fast-track development and build your skills to confidently step into a future leadership position!
