title: Arabic Consecutive Linguist
description:
UNLEASH YOUR POTENTIAL

At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

Are you ready for your next career challenge? Ready to see the World?

THE MISSION


Leidos has an exciting potential future opportunity for an Arabic Consecutive Linguist based in Arlington, VA. We are proactively looking to identify highly qualified linguists to support a DoD customer in the National Capital Region (NCR), with extensive travel to Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. The linguist will provide language support services including interpretation, translation, and transcription in assisting defense counsels with interviews of detainees and witnesses for court rooms and case preparation for Military Commissions hearings that are held in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. Interested candidates must already possess a current TS/SCI security clearance.

Are you ready to make an impact? Begin a flourishing and meaningful career, share your resume with us today!

THE CHALLENGE

The Arabic Linguist will support the Leidos Defense Sector and be assigned to a defense legal team conducting interviews of detainee and witnesses for court rooms and case preparation for the Military Commissions hearings held in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. The linguist will provide interpretation, translation, and transcription of discovery material. Place of performance shall vary with requirements. The places of performance will be the National Capital Region (NCR) and a significant amount of the work will occur at the Office of Military Commissions (OMC) deployed facility at US Naval Station, Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, and some other overseas locations. Additional work shall be performed on site at the OMC facilities in the National Capital Region.


WHAT YOU’LL DO:

The Linguist will be assigned to specific legal defense team performing various functions including but not limited to:

  • Review general and technical source material in the Arabic language to prepare accurate written translations, and/or transcriptions in idiomatic English.

  • Provide interpretation, translation, and transcription support to include assisting defense counsels with interviews of detainees and witnesses.

  • Interpret in the consecutive mode required by the setting and reproduce the original message after the speaker pauses, such as in the “question and answer” mode in which the speaker completes his statement and the interpreter begins to interpret after the statement is completed.

  • Translate the full meaning of a written text from one language to another. Provide accurate and thorough translations from English into Arabic language or from a Arabic language into English of documents as provided by the defense legal teams.

  • Transcribe audio/video discovery material into English.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING (REQUIRED):

  • 5+ years of related work experience

  • BA/BS and or equivalent formal military training or related experience will be considered in lieu of degree.

  • Must be available for 60% travel.

  • Achieve a minimum score of an Interagency Language Roundtable (ILR) 3 in Arabic

  • and 3 in English for Reading, Listening, Speaking, and Writing, with a preference given to a 3+.

  • Demonstrated history of working on translation projects and in maintaining the integrity and meaning of the translated material.

  • Ability to conduct and prepare accurate translation, and/or transcriptions of general and technical legal materials.

  • Ability to write and speak in a clear, concise, and professional manner in the Arabic and English.

  • Ability to provide written translation of documents with error free in a gist, detailed summary, or full translation format utilizing approved templates and dictionaries in the time allotted, while maintaining the integrity and meaning of material.

  • Ability to write and speak clearly and coherently in Arabic and English.

  • Ability to read a variety of unfamiliar subjects, relate ideas, make intelligent inferences, and rarely misunderstand the intent of the writer.

  • Ability to accurately format, proofread, edit, apply graphic designs, and other software functions needed to meet customer product expectations.

  • Ability to translate or interpret conversations accurately and clearly.

  • Ability to consistently deliver a quality product within the established standards.

  • Ability to meet and strive to exceed minimum production levels and standards in number of pages translated.

  • Be proficient in MS Office programs (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and be computer literate.

  • Ability to deploy to Guantanamo Bay, Cuba and other overseas locations on short notice for an extended period, staying in housing based on availability for Commission hearings and for investigative and case preparation work, and will be required to attend all sessions of trial, seated at the defense table.

  • Ability to interact positively with Leidos government customer and co-workers at all times.

  • Team player who is able to communicate effectively with colleagues, addresses tasks quickly and efficiently, and collaborates on group projects.

  • Willing to work long hours to meet mission demands.

  • Sufficient technical aptitude to gain a working knowledge on job-required tools and processes.

CLEARANCE: Must currently possess a minimum TS/SCI in DISS.

title: Vice President, Retail Media Measurements & Insights
description:
What You'll Do:

About the Role

Criteo is a global commerce media company, enabling marketers and media owners to deliver richer consumer experiences and drive better commerce outcomes through our industry-leading Commerce Media Platform. Retail Media is one of our fastest-growing businesses, and measurement is central to how we earn advertiser trust and grow alongside our clients.

As advertisers raise the bar from correlation to causation, credible and transparent measurement has become one of the most important ways a commerce media platform demonstrates its value. A key part of Criteo’s strength is our ability to show a brand’s performance across more than 200 retailers — a perspective that is difficult to find anywhere else.

As VP, Retail Media Measurement & Insights, you will set the vision for how Criteo measures Retail Media performance and turns that measurement into insight that strengthens client relationships and drives growth. This is a leadership role centered on measurement standards, client-facing insight strategy, and commercial enablement.

You will lead the Insights Partners team and partner closely with Product (which owns the measurement and insights roadmap and platform delivery), along with Commercial (which owns the client relationship), to bring industry-leading measurement and insights to market.

What You’ll Do

Lead client-facing measurement and insights

  • Lead and develop the Insights Partners team as Criteo’s senior, client-facing measurement and insights experts, engaging brands, agencies, and retailers in strategic measurement conversations.
  • Serve as a credible external voice for Criteo’s measurement approach and methodologies with senior client and industry audiences.
  • Translate measurement into client value — building advertiser confidence and supporting renewals, growth, retailer partnerships, and agency engagement — while Account Strategists continue to own day-to-day campaign strategy, insights, and execution.

Define measurement standards and framework

  • Define, champion, and continuously evolve Retail Media’s common measurement framework across the areas advertisers care about most — attribution, competitive position, incrementality, customer health, and brand health — aligned to standards that brands and agencies trust.
  • Set the measurement standards that Criteo’s Retail Media analytics, reporting, and in-platform insights align to — for example, the accepted methodology for incrementality testing, common definitions for metrics such as incremental sales and iROAS, agreed attribution windows, and the criteria a metric must meet to be considered validated and client-ready.

Enable commercial teams

  • Equip Commercial teams with the narrative, proof points, and frameworks to bring Criteo’s measurement and insights story to market consistently, including our differentiated cross-retailer perspective.
  • Support pipeline, renewals, and growth through a clear, repeatable measurement story and senior client engagement where it matters most.

Shape build-versus-partner and validation strategy

  • Provide market and client inputs to Product’s build-versus-partner decisions — identifying unmet needs, assessing potential partner capabilities, and validating where partnerships could complement Criteo’s product roadmap.
  • Lead Criteo’s validation approach so measurement is independently credible — accredited where required, validated by neutral partners where trust demands it, and compatible with the tools clients prefer to use.
  • Position Criteo as a trusted commerce-media input to the marketing mix models that brands and agencies already run, and pursue partnerships for brand lift, clean-room collaboration, and identity and LTV enrichment.
  • Identify and develop external measurement and data partnerships, working alongside Criteo’s Corporate Development and Partnerships teams, as the measurement subject-matter authority.

Lead with a global perspective

  • Bring a global lens across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC, recognizing that advertiser expectations, competitive dynamics, and privacy requirements differ by region, and tailoring standards and client engagement accordingly.

Champion trusted data practices

  • Establish clear principles for how data is used within Retail Media, including data rights and trust standards, with privacy-safe data collaboration as a foundation.
  • Bring fluency in global privacy requirements and translate them into what measurement is possible in each region.

Represent Retail Media across the company

  • Represent Retail Media’s measurement and insights perspective in broader company initiatives, helping define where alignment across the business creates advertiser value.

Who You Are:

  • A senior leader with 15+ years of experience who has owned measurement and insights strategy at scale in retail or commerce media, ad platforms, or a measurement or data provider. Agency experience is highly preferred.
  • Deep, current expertise in commerce-media measurement — incrementality (holdout, in-auction/ghost-bidding, page lift), attribution, marketing mix modeling, brand lift, and clean rooms — with a strong grasp of the trust-and-validation landscape, such as MRC accreditation, neutral incrementality providers, and IAB standards.
  • Proven experience leading senior, client-facing consultative teams and turning measurements into commercial outcomes such as renewals, growth, and advertiser confidence.
  • Skilled at collaborating across Product, Commercial, Account Strategy, Analytics, Legal, and Privacy — setting direction and standards while partnering effectively without owning execution.
  • A track record of driving cross-functional alignment and shaping company-level decisions.
  • Experienced in navigating both retailer and advertiser dynamics.
  • Globally fluent across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC, including GDPR and regional privacy requirements.
  • Experienced with data governance and related processes.
  • A credible external representative for Criteo — comfortable engaging senior agency and brand audiences and speaking at industry forums — with a track record of building external measurement and data partnerships.

We acknowledge that many candidates may not meet every single role requirement listed above. If your experience looks a little different from our requirements but you believe that you can still bring value to the role, we’d love to see your application!​

Who We Are:

We’re Criteo, the Commerce Intelligence Platform. Criteo helps businesses turn shopper signals into commerce outcomes while delivering more relevant experiences for shoppers. We use proprietary commerce intelligence and AI decisioning to drive relevance for shoppers and performance for businesses.

At Criteo, our culture is as unique as it is diverse. From our offices across the globe or from the comfort of home, our 3,600 Criteos collaborate together to build an open, impactful, and forward-thinking environment.

We foster a workplace where everyone is valued, and employment decisions are based solely on skills, qualifications, and business needs—never on non-job-related factors or legally protected characteristics.

What We Offer:

🏢 Ways of working – Our hybrid model blends home with in-office experiences, making space for both.
📈 Grow with us – Learning, mentorship & career development programs.
💪 Your wellbeing matters – Health benefits, wellness perks & mental health support.
🤝 A team that cares – Diverse, inclusive, and globally connected.
💸 Fair pay & perks – Attractive salary, with performance-based rewards and family-friendly policies, plus the potential for equity depending on role and level.

Additional benefits may vary depending on the country where you work and the nature of your employment with Criteo.

For employees based in the US, certain roles at Criteo are eligible for additional rewards, including quarterly or annual bonus and restricted stock units. US-based employees receive access to healthcare, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, short-term and long-term disability coverage, life insurance, family forming and wellness benefits, Flexible Work financial support, learning opportunities, and a robust annual leave plan including volunteer time off and summer vacation days.

The tester contributes to test case development, test automation, defect reporting, and continuous improvement while learning established testing standards, security practices, and delivery processes.

title: OPICS Partner Fellow
description:
Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world.

Requirements

Job Overview

The Fellow will work in the Georgetown Center on Poverty & Inequality through Georgetown Law’s Partner Fellowship program. Under the supervision of a Senior Policy Analyst, the Fellow will engage in law-related work that may include, but is not limited to: conducting research; writing memos and other reports; organizing and presenting at conferences and meetings; engaging with the media; coordinating with coalition partners; conducting policy advocacy and public education; and assisting with operational and administrative functions.

The Georgetown Center on Poverty and Inequality’s Economic Security and Opportunity Initiative (ESOI) works with policymakers, researchers, practitioners, and advocates to develop effective policies and practices to alleviate poverty and inequality in the United States. Areas of research include policies, programs, and practices related to tax and benefits, jobs and education, health and human service delivery, and democracy, all with a cross-cutting focus on racial and gender equity.

The Partner Fellow will conduct research and policy analysis: identifying policy issues to explore, collecting and analyzing data, reporting findings, and proposing new ideas for addressing problems on a wide range of issues relating to economic security and opportunity. Fellow will

  • Conduct policy research on pending legislation and regulations, existing laws and policies, and new policy ideas and proposals;
  • Draft and promote papers, articles, fact sheets, briefs, blog posts, op-eds, and social media content;
  • Collaborate with advocates, policy experts, policymakers, media, and other stakeholders.

Work Interactions

The Fellow reports directly to the Senior Policy Analyst. The Fellow will have interaction with students, faculty and support offices on the Law Center’s campus, in addition to external partners and stakeholders.

Requirements and Qualifications

The position is open to individuals who have received or will receive a Juris Doctor during the most recent academic year. Coursework relevant to the Center or Institute is preferred. Position requires a commitment to GCPI’s mission, excellent research, writing & verbal communication skills, education or experience with policy analysis and research, and basic proficiency in MS Excel (includes ability to enter, correct, and filter data, apply functions in formulas, format worksheets, and work with charts).

The ideal candidate has:

*Professional, academic and lived experience with issues related to poverty, economic justice, social inclusion, racial equity, and gender equity

*Knowledge of a broad range of economic security issues

*Self-driven work ethic & initiative and strong capacity for collaboration

Job Description

The Associate Director of Scholarship manages the university’s Foundation Scholarship Program to ensure effective scholarship program administration. Responsibilities include participating in the development of scholarships (including working with the fundraising staff on criteria, writing of drafts, ensuring award-ability and input into the software), managing the scholarship software, developing communications, supporting students through the application and awarding process, and providing guidance to application reviewers. The position builds and maintains collaborative relationships across the division, with campus partners such as Financial Aid and Admissions, and with external stakeholders advance the university’s scholarship strategy.

Responsibilities:

1. Scholarship System. Serve as the university expert for the award management software and direct the university's utilization of the tool.

  • Make sure all new scholarship agreements are executed and uploaded.
  • Guide stakeholders on how to utilize the software to administer scholarship dollars.
  • Ensure scholarship system data accurately reflects awarding parameters agreed upon with benefactors.
  • Utilize the system to advertise and process recruitment and other university scholarships.
  • Provide training and guidance to support application reviews and award offers.
  • Serve as the liaison with WSU IT and the scholarship software vendor to troubleshoot and integrate enhancement in the system.

2. Scholarship Strategy. Manage the scholarship program to maximize utilization of student scholarship funds.

  • Collaborate with Advancement team members and benefactors to develop and implement scholarships that meaningfully represent the benefactors’ philanthropic goals and adhere to applicable policies, procedures and laws.
  • Promote the scholarship program to students, parents, and other stakeholders, including Admissions, Financial Aid, Equity and Inclusive Excellence, and academic departments.
  • Ensure scholarship application evaluators are identified, trained, and complete application reviews.
  • Collaborate with other departments to gather and share sensitive information necessary to verify student eligibility.
  • Support the WSU Foundation Scholarship Committee by supporting committee operations, including agenda development, meeting scheduling, minute preparation, and follow-up on action items.
  • Creation of the scholarship documents with input from the fundraising staff.
  • Maintaining the hard copies of the executed scholarship documents.
  • Assist with the annual allocation from each scholarship with the Foundation Controller, Executive Director and the VP of University Advancement.

3. Stewardship and Donor Engagement. Develop and maintain relationships to support scholarship award sustainability and growth.

  • Provide guidance to prospective donors acting as a gatekeeper for WSU fundraising team.
  • Ensure scholarship benefactors receive individualized recognition and expressions of gratitude from the university. Example would be the student thank you initiative.
  • Foster meaningful connections between scholarship recipients and benefactors through letters, events, classroom speaking opportunities, and other engagement activities including an annual scholarship event.
  • Represent the division at key events that promote donor engagement.

4. Scholarship Budget. Maintain budget and data needs related to the scholarship plan.

  • Communicate with the Foundation Controller to ensure adequate funding is available prior to posting available scholarships.
  • Collaborate with the Executive Director to contact benefactors to solicit additional contributions or obtain guidance regarding awarding preferences in cases of insufficient funding.
  • Collaborate with the Executive Director, Controller and VP of Advancement to use data-informed decision-making in the awarding and disbursement of scholarships.
  • Collaborate with the Controller to monitor expenditures and maintain monthly records of endowment and account balances to ensure responsible stewardship of dollars.

5. Emergency Grant Program. Collaborate with the university emergency grant program administrator. Be the liaison between the university emergency grant administrator and the WSU Foundation.

6. Perform other duties as assigned to ensure the smooth functioning of the department and maintain the reputation of Winona State University. Including but not limited to participating in university committees and pursuing ongoing professional development to maintain current knowledge in the field.

Job Posting Title: Senior Therapeutic Area Specialist, Cardiovascular Community - San Diego, CA

At Bristol Myers Squibb, we are inspired by a single vision – transforming patients’ lives through science. The BMS Mission is to discover, develop and deliver innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases. In oncology, hematology, immunology and cardiovascular disease – and one of the most diverse and promising pipelines in the industry – each of our passionate colleagues contribute to innovations that drive meaningful change. We bring a human touch to every treatment we pioneer.

Join us, build your professional career within one of the most innovative bio-pharma companies, and make a difference.

Position Summary

The TAS is a critical role in our unique customer model to execute the BMS aspiration to be the BioPharma that delivers the most impactful engagement with Health Care Providers (HCPs), driving adoption of new and existing medicines for appropriate patients.

The primary role of the TAS is to drive demand for BMS medicines within their portfolio for the appropriate patients. To meet the HCPs expectations, the TAS engages them with a differentiated Customer Experience (Cx) through deeper scientific dialogue on and consistent with label, leveraging new ways of working and CE^3.

The role builds and maintains strong professional credibility with regional thought leaders (RTLs) and community-based physicians/HCPs in private practice, medical groups practices, office staff, and other stakeholders in the patient care continuum as their primary point of contact.

The TAS liaises with other BMS functions as needed to deliver an overall higher Customer Experience (Cx) – by meeting HCP needs in a timely and scientific manner. This role will prioritize the safe and appropriate use of BMS products while also focusing on overall business results and performance objectives while exemplifying BMS values.

The TAS role is field-based. A TAS is anticipated to spend much of their time spent field with external customers.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Promotion

  • Promotes approved indications of BMS products within a defined territory or region to meet or exceed assigned sales targets in a compliant manner.

  • Creates demand for BMS medicines by articulating in a balanced manner the clinical and scientific rationale for use of products in appropriate patients.

  • Engages with and continuously maintains/grows a high level of scientific expertise in all assigned products and therapeutic areas.

  • Prepares and successfully implements comprehensive territory and account plans.

  • Proactively uses available tools such as SOPHIA to derive insights and to dynamically inform call plans.

  • Provides feedback on experience using these tools to leadership to enable continuous improvement.

Fair & Balanced Scientific Dialogue

  • Demonstrates scientific expertise and passion in using approved scientific resources and publications to present information to HCPs and ensures medical accuracy.

  • Conducts in-office presentations (e.g., lunch and learns) and discusses product-related scientific information with HCPs that is consistent with label.

  • Organizes external speaker programs, selecting speakers from list approved by Speakers Bureau and facilitating scheduling and logistics.

  • Maintains a high level of working expertise on emerging data for approved indications.

  • Engages real-time medical support through Medical on Call to reactively answer unsolicited questions and complex technical inquiries.

Cross-functional collaboration

  • Proactively collaborates with other field teams to ensure the best Customer Experience (Cx) for HCPs.

  • Gathers and shares relevant insights and information internally with the appropriate stakeholders to enable BMS to better serve its customers.

Complies with all laws, regulations, and policies that govern the conduct of BMS.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Advanced scientific degree and/or preferred 5+ years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology experience as healthcare sales / MSL / HCP / nurse.

  • Ability to communicate scientific or clinical data accurately and convincingly to help physicians best serve their patients.

  • Demonstrated experience building and maintaining strong credibility with key customers, office staff, and others in the customer influence network via a customer-centric mindset and desire to create positive and differentiated Customer Experience (Cx).

  • Experience in cardiovascular preferred.

  • Demonstrated strong capability in account management skill sets, superior selling competencies, and proven sales performance track record of meeting or exceeding goals.

  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functionally with a positive team mindset and can-do attitude.

  • Strong selling and promotional skills proven through a track record of performance.

Key competencies desired

Customer/commercial mindset

  • Demonstrated ability to drive business results.

  • Experience identifying, engaging, and cultivating credibility with customers across the patient care journey.

  • Demonstrated account management skills and problem-solving mentality. Understands the patient journey and can customize engagement and deliver tailored messages.

  • Demonstrated resourcefulness and ability to connect with customers.

Patient centricity

  • Understands the patient journey and experience.

  • Has a patient-focused mindset.

Scientific Agility

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills to articulate scientific and clinical data in an easy-to-understand manner to help HCPs best serve their patients.

  • Has a strong learning mindset and passion for science. Prioritizes staying current with the latest data.

Analytical Capability:

  • Ability to analyze data, such as prescribing patterns, market trends, and HCP preferences. Data-driven insights help TAS strategize and target their efforts effectively.

  • Ability to segment HCPs based on their preferences and other relevant factors. This helps them tailor their communication and product presentations to suit individual HCP needs.

  • Understanding how to interpret and analyze data related to BMS products, customer preferences, clinical data.

  • Ability to use CE^3 to generate insights and do dynamic call planning.

Digital Agility:

  • Understanding, adapting, and effectively using technology in various aspects of healthcare business and interacting with HCPs.

  • Utilizing various digital communication channels such as emails, instant messaging apps, and video conferencing to stay in touch with healthcare professionals, colleagues, and clients. This enables TAS to respond promptly to inquiries, share updates, and maintain effective communication.

  • Competency using CE^3 and other software or CRM tools to collect, enter, and manage quality data in a timely and compliant manner, track interactions, and plan future engagements with healthcare professionals.

  • Ability to use the Medical on Call technology effectively.

  • Keeping up to date with technological advancements and changes.

Teamwork/Enterprise mindset

  • Strong business acumen to understand and analyze business, market drivers, and develop, execute, and adjust business plans.

  • Demonstrates a strong sense of learning agility. Seeks out and learns from unfamiliar experiences, and then applies those lessons to achieve better results in subsequent situations.

  • Track record of balancing individual drive and collaborative attitude.

  • Holds a high level of integrity and good judgment to navigate the role's requirements effectively and compliantly in accordance with BMS policies and procedures.

As this position requires the operation of a Company-provided vehicle, offers of employment are contingent upon the candidate meeting the requirements of “Qualified Driver,” as determined by the Company in its sole discretion, including but not limited to the following: 1) at least 21 years of age; 2) a driver’s license in good standing issued by your state of residence; and, 3) a driving risk level deemed acceptable by the Company.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Leidos Defense is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join our team in our San Diego facility, supporting the U.S. Navy’s AN/SQQ-89(V) Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) systems.

Our program helps modernize Navy ships by replacing outdated sonar systems with updated AN/SQQ-89(V)15 systems, supporting the installation, logistics, quality checks, and training needed to prepare ship personnel to operate the new systems.

In this role, you will focus on modernizing the AN/SQQ-89(V) ASW Training System by transitioning Tactical Insertion (TI) hardware-based solutions to a scalable, virtualized Linux training platform. You’ll work with Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), KVM, Open vSwitch, Python, Ansible, and hardware passthrough technologies to support complex Navy training and simulation environments.

What You'll Do

  • Design, deploy, and maintain virtualized environments supporting AN/SQQ-89(V)15 training capabilities.

  • Migrate software and services from Tactical Insertion hardware platforms to virtualized environments using KVM, libvirt, virsh, and VirtIO.

  • Build and maintain RHEL 7/8 system images, templates, and repositories.

  • Develop automated deployment and configuration solutions using Ansible.

  • Create Python utilities and scripts for system administration, testing, monitoring, and data management.

  • Configure and maintain Open vSwitch environments supporting multiple networks and high-throughput virtual machine communications.

  • Integrate physical and virtual networking within tactical training environments.

  • Troubleshoot complex virtualization, Linux, networking, storage, hardware, and application integration issues.

  • Support performance tuning and optimization of virtualized systems, networking, storage, and compute resources.

  • Support software integration, system verification, validation, and acceptance testing.

  • Collaborate with software developers, systems engineers, cybersecurity personnel, and training system stakeholders.

  • Support cybersecurity compliance activities, including STIG implementation, vulnerability remediation, and RMF activities.

  • Develop and maintain architecture diagrams, deployment guides, standard operating procedures, and automation documentation.

  • Support modernization efforts focused on improving the portability, scalability, and maintainability of training environments.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree with 4–8 years of relevant experience, or a Master's degree with 2–6 years of relevant experience.

  • Experience with Linux systems engineering, virtualization, software development, or platform engineering.

  • Experience administering Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) environments.

  • Strong experience with KVM, libvirt, and virsh.

  • Experience implementing and troubleshooting Open vSwitch (OVS).

  • Experience with hardware passthrough technologies, including PCIe passthrough, VFIO, SR-IOV, and IOMMU configuration.

  • Experience developing infrastructure automation using Ansible.

  • Experience developing software and automation tools using Python.

  • Strong understanding of Linux networking concepts, including VLANs, bridges, routing, bonding, and virtual switching.

  • Experience troubleshooting integration issues across hardware, operating systems, networking, and applications.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting AN/SQQ-89(V)15 or AEGIS combat systems.

  • Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE).

  • Experience with high-performance networking and low-latency virtualized environments.

  • Experience supporting GPU, FPGA, capture card, or other specialized hardware passthrough to virtual machines.

  • Familiarity with distributed storage, NFS, iSCSI, and SAN technologies.

  • Experience with FreeIPA, LDAP, Kerberos, and enterprise Linux identity management.

  • Experience supporting RMF, STIG implementation, ACAS, and cybersecurity compliance initiatives.

  • Active Secret or Top Secret clearance.

If you have a strong Linux and virtualization background and are interested in applying those skills to modernize U.S. Navy training systems, we encourage you to apply.

title: Group Statutory Controller
description:
ABOUT TEMENOS


Temenos is a global leader in banking technology. Through our market-leading core banking suite and best-in-class composable solutions, we are modernizing the banking industry. Banks of all sizes utilize our adaptable technology – on-premises, in the cloud, or as SaaS – to deliver next-generation services and AI-enhanced experiences that elevate banking for their customers. Commit to being part of an exciting culture and product evolving within the financial industry.

Challenge yourself to be ambitious and achieve your individual as well as the company targets.


The Group Statutory Controller will be a key member of the group finance team, reporting directly to the Head of Group Reporting and Group Accountant. They will oversee the local statutory accounts reporting process across the group, working with local statutory controllers and auditors to ensure consistent delivery of timely and high quality statutory reporting under relevant local accounting standard.

They will also drive operational excellence in the statutory reporting process, identifying areas for improvement in the statutory control environment and intercompany process.

OPPORTUNITIES

  • You will work closely with local statutory controllers to ensure timely delivery of subsidiary statutory accounts to meet local reporting and borrowing covenant deadlines
  • You will provide technical support to local statutory controllers on preparation of local statutory accounts, including goodwill/intangible asset impairment reviews and accounting for investments and intercompany balances
  • You will develop strong working relationship with local external auditors to ensure smooth audit process and minimize audit issues
  • You will act as a key point of contact for local statutory controllers, identifying common reporting/control issues and implementing solutions together with the group finance team
  • You will communicate reporting issues on a timely basis to the Head of Group Reporting and work with the group finance and local finance team to resolve issues identified
  • You will oversee reconciliation process between local statutory and group reported numbers, and drive improvements in the timeliness and accuracy of the reconciliation process
  • You will coordinate with local controllers, treasury and group finance team to identify and drive improvements to intercompany accounting process, including mitigation of material FX exposures and settlement of intercompany positions
  • You will work closely with Head of Group Reporting on any other ad hoc activities and projects

REQUIREMENTS

  • You should be a qualified accountant (ACA / ACCA) with proven experience of working in multi-national reporting environment
  • You should have proven organizational, written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with ability to interact at all staff levels
  • You should be fast and responsive – working to tight deadlines
  • You should be a team player, maintaining close working relationship with relevant teams across the group
  • You should have good analytical skills and close attention to detail
  • You should have up to date knowledge of IFRS reporting and proven track record on preparation/sign off of statutory accounts
  • You should have exposure to consolidation / Multi currency / Intercompany positions
  • You should have exposure of Oracle ERP system

Job Title

Gong Administrator (Business System Analyst – Staff A)

Work Location: Sky tech, Financial District, Hyderabad, India

Key Responsibilities

  • Define and maintain an ownership/RACI model for Gong administration between IT and CS Ops to eliminate ambiguity and ensure smooth onboarding and support.

  • Own Gong user lifecycle management (provisioning/deprovisioning, role assignment, access reviews, and least-privilege access).

  • Provide key data insights and reporting to stakeholders, reviewing and analyzing trends

  • Deliver end-to-end CRM integration (setup, authentication, permissions alignment, ongoing maintenance), including the Gong integration user model and access controls required for CRM data ingestion/export.

  • Troubleshoot integration issues and manage coordination with internal CRM admins and Gong Support as needed.

  • Ability to collaborate with cross functional team deliver outcomes within the agreed OLA/SLA.

  • Support new user onboarding with training, access management, permission sets.

  • Ensure administration actions follow internal security guardrails—especially for settings that affect user access and system configuration.

  • Support User/training issues resolved via guidance and internal enablement materials.

  • Maintain internal support documentation/FAQ and standard operating procedures for consistent support outcomes.

  • Partner with business stakeholders to implement platform changes that enable reporting, scorecards, exports, and business workflows—while keeping configuration changes controlled and auditable.

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Seasonal Mosquito Technicians do?

The primary purpose of this role is to provide a quality, professional service. They deliver service with courtesy, safety, and dependability and to ensure each customer has a positive experience. Here at VDCI, we have a strong focus on preventing the spread of diseases through mosquito control. We complete mosquito surveillance and preventative services, as well as large-scale spraying.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Routinely inspect control zones for potential mosquito breeding habitat and the presence of mosquito larvae by visual inspection and “dipping”

  • Assess each inspection site and utilize the appropriate control techniques, such as: no action, source reduction, biological control, public education and chemical control (including the application of larvicides and/ adulticides at the labeled application rates)

  • May place and retrieve monitoring devices for accessing mosquito populations

  • Accurately record all findings and control activities on the appropriate log sheet and GPS unit, and enter data into VDCI’s database as required by the contract

  • Be thoroughly familiar with all applicable chemical labels and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and handle/apply all chemicals according to label specifications

  • Know and follow proper safety and spill procedures at all times, and use all required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) regularly.

  • Communicate respectfully, honestly, and knowledgeably to residents at all times during service request inspections, routine larvicide activities, or during any other public relations activities

  • Know and follow the proper and safe operations of all equipment used,

  • Mix pesticides & fill sprayers accurately as needed, and follow all required safety precautions for the application of products

  • React to change promptly and effectively, and handle other essential tasks as assigned.

  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills and the ability to present information in both internal and external settings.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Comfortable with self-directed working conditions after a training period

  • Work is regularly performed outdoors and may include exposure to potentially hazardous situations and substances such as weather conditions, challenging and uneven/unstable terrain, pesticides, dust and airborne particulates, excessive noise, biting insects, hazardous plants, and wild and domestic animals.

  • Must be capable of lifting and using items such as chemical containers and application equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.

  • Safely operate a motor vehicle and make sure it and all other equipment is kept clean.

What do you need?

  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in the area of pest control

  • High school diploma or GED; related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Possess a valid driver’s license from state of residence.

title: Test Engineer
description:

The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. Join us as a Test Engineer, at Barclays, where you will spearhead the evolution of our infrastructure and deployment pipelines, driving innovation and operational excellence. You will harness cutting-edge technology to build and manage robust, scalable and secure infrastructure, ensuring seamless delivery of our digital solutions.

To be successful as a Test Engineer, you should have experience with:

  • Experience in both Manual and Automation Testing.

Some other highly valued skills may include:

  • Ability to identify positive, negative, edge-case, and comprehensive test coverage scenarios.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Proactive and self-driven mindset.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder collaboration skills.
  • Prior Barclays, Cards, or Payments domain preferred experience.

title: AI Learning Product Owner
description:
Job Description

To design and implement programmes and initiatives that support the growth and development of the bank’s employees and leaders.

They may also lead a number of specialists to influence the operations of a department, in alignment with strategic as well as tactical priorities, while balancing short and long term goals and ensuring that budgets and schedules meet corporate requirements..
  • If the position has leadership responsibilities, People Leaders are expected to demonstrate a clear set of leadership behaviours to create an environment for colleagues to thrive and deliver to a consistently excellent standard. The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others..
  • OR for an individual contributor, they will be a subject matter expert within own discipline and will guide technical direction. They will lead collaborative, multi-year assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will train, guide and coach less experienced specialists and provide information affecting long term profits, organisational risks and strategic decisions..
  • Advise key stakeholders, including functional leadership teams and senior management on functional and cross functional areas of impact and alignment.
  • Manage and mitigate risks through assessment, in support of the control and governance agenda.
  • Demonstrate leadership and accountability for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work your team does.
  • Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the organisation functions to contribute to achieving the goals of the business.
  • Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategies.
  • Create solutions based on sophisticated analytical thought comparing and selecting complex alternatives. In-depth analysis with interpretative thinking will be required to define problems and develop innovative solutions.
  • Adopt and include the outcomes of extensive research in problem solving processes.
  • Seek out, build and maintain trusting relationships and partnerships with internal and external stakeholders in order to accomplish key business objectives, using influencing and negotiating skills to achieve outcomes.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

Join Barclays as an AI Product Owner. This is a role leading the design, deployment and continuous improvement of enterprise-wide AI learning products. The role will work closely with technical teams and key stakeholders to shape the product roadmap, translate business needs into scalable solutions, and drive adoption of AI-enabled learning across the bank.

To be successful in this role you should have experience in the following:

  • Defining and owning the vision, roadmap and priorities for enterprise-wide AI learning products, ensuring alignment to talent, learning and business priorities.

  • Translating talent development needs into clear product requirements, user stories and release plans that can be delivered by technical teams.

  • Working closely with learning, HR, technology, data and risk stakeholders to prioritise features, manage trade-offs and ensure solutions are valuable, feasible and secure.

  • Leading product deployment and adoption, ensuring AI learning products are implemented effectively and deliver a strong colleague experience.

  • Monitoring product performance, user feedback and business outcomes to drive continuous improvement, optimisation and scale.

  • Staying on current AI, learning technology and product management trends to identify opportunities to enhance enterprise learning products and ways of working.

You may be assessed on the key critical skills relevant for success in role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen strategic thinking and digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills.

title: Project Scientist (GeoSystems Analysis)
description:
GeoSystems Analysis, Inc., a Trinity Consultants team, is seeking a Project Scientist to join our growing team in the southwest. The Project Scientist performs scientific and technical work supporting environmental consulting projects related to mine closure, heap leach hydrodynamics, managed aquifer recharge, and riparian habitat restoration. This position collects, analyzes, and interprets field and laboratory data; supports hydrologic and geologic investigations; and assists with technical evaluations, modeling, and reporting. The Project Scientist works collaboratively with multidisciplinary project teams to develop practical, science-based solutions for domestic and international clients while supporting field investigations, environmental monitoring, and project execution. While ideally based in Tucson, AZ, candidates that are local to our other Trinity offices in the West are encouraged to apply.

What will I be doing?

  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams led by technical experts specializing in mine closure, heap leach hydrodynamics, managed aquifer recharge, riparian habitat restoration, groundwater and surface water modeling, and remote/UAV data acquisition.
  • Support mine closure projects involving tailings storage facilities, heap leach pads, waste rock facilities, reclamation landforms, cover system design, and stormwater management.
  • Assist with mine water balance evaluations for tailings, heap leach, and waste rock facilities.
  • Collect, analyze, and interpret physical, hydraulic, hydrologic, and geochemical data to evaluate fluid flow and contaminant transport within mine waste and heap leach facilities.
  • Conduct field investigations including borehole drilling oversight, monitoring well installation, vadose zone instrumentation, groundwater and surface water sampling, monitoring activities, and UAV-based data collection.
  • Support installation, operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of large-scale environmental monitoring systems.
  • Analyze laboratory and field data using statistical, geospatial, and hydrologic methods to develop technically sound conclusions and recommendations.
  • Prepare technical reports, memoranda, data summaries, figures, and presentations for clients and regulatory agencies.
  • Participate in field assignments at remote domestic and international project locations while maintaining a strong commitment to safety.
  • Build and maintain positive working relationships with clients, regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and project team members.
  • Support project planning, scheduling, budgeting, and quality assurance activities as experience and responsibilities increase.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

What qualifications are required for this role?

  • Bachelor's degree in Hydrogeology, Geosciences, Soil Science, Geology, Hydrology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field required.
  • Master's degree in Hydrogeology, Geosciences, Soil Science, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of relevant research, consulting, or applied environmental science experience.
  • Experience supporting mine closure, mine water management, hydrologic investigations, environmental monitoring, or related environmental consulting projects preferred.
  • Previous experience performing fieldwork under physically demanding or remote conditions is considered an asset.
  • Strong understanding of hydrogeologic, geologic, soil science, and hydrologic principles.
  • Ability to collect, organize, analyze, interpret, and communicate complex scientific and technical data.
  • Preferred experience in GIS analysis, programming (Python), numerical modeling, field data collection, and data analysis/report writing.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to project sites in the Western U.S. and/or internationally.
  • Experience with groundwater flow and transport modeling software such as MODFLOW or HYDRUS is preferred.
  • Fluency (written and spoken) in Spanish is preferred.

The salary range for this position is $75,000 - $95,000 per year. In addition, Geosystems Analysis has a discretionary bonus program that considers business profitability and individual performance.

What does GSA offer you?

  • Comprehensive benefits package: 9 paid holidays, healthcare benefits, PTO, and 401k matching for full-time employees.
  • Multidisciplinary environment: Unique, creative, and challenging projects where you can develop your vision of clientele and work with industry leaders daily.
  • Success-oriented environment: Two-way mentorship, tuition reimbursement, and a career path structure to help you reach the next steps in your career.
  • Collaborative work environment: Clear and frequent communication, shared information and ideas across teams, and a welcoming atmosphere for everyone.

With more than 60,000 employees worldwide, the company has a strong industrial presence in Italy, the United Kingdom, Poland, and the United States, and operates in 150 countries through subsidiaries, joint ventures, and equity investments. title: Certified Recovery Specialst
description:
St. Luke's is proud of the skills, experience and compassion of its employees. The employees of St. Luke's are our most valuable asset! Individually and together, our employees are dedicated to satisfying the mission of our organization which is an unwavering commitment to excellence as we care for the sick and injured; educate physicians, nurses and other health care providers; and improve access to care in the communities we serve, regardless of a patient's ability to pay for health care.

Hours: Full-Time

The CRS has experience with behavioral health services and is willing to use and share lived experiences and first-hand knowledge to hospital patients, their family members, and staff. The CRS functions as a substance use resource and liaison to Network Emergency Departments, medical inpatient units, and all staff to provide expertise around community resources, the recovery process, symptom management, and the persistence needed by patients/families to have a recovery oriented and satisfying life. The CRS works to identify engagement needs and helps to work with individuals through stages of change. The CRS helps the patient and family identify opportunities from a strength-based approach about enhancing life domain needs. The CRS works collaboratively with Network interdisciplinary teams to provide education on stigma, resources, and lived experiences.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Engage in relationship building and active listening with patients receiving treatment in emergency room, medical inpatient units or virtually who have a substance use disorder.
  • Utilize best practices such as motivational interviewing and stages of change to assist individuals in healthcare decision making related to substance use disorder recovery.
  • Provide supportive (peer-based) coaching and encouragement to patients contemplating or actively seeking help with substance use treatment and recovery. Ensuring that all interactions are strength-based, recovery oriented and understanding of multiple pathways and definitions of recovery.
  • Provide education to enable patients to identify their relapse symptoms or relapse triggers as well as their protective factors (to avoid relapse).
  • Engage and provide education to family members, other natural supports, and other professionals regarding substance use disorders and available programs/resources.
  • Assist in after-care planning for individuals discharging from medical setting and help ensure that behavioral health needs are included in care plan.
  • Engage in team-based care and work cooperatively with other medical professionals.
  • Engage and develop education sessions regarding recovery and stigma awareness to medical professionals, and other stakeholders.
  • Complete appropriate documentation, including to document each service-related contact in case note according to program standards.
  • Keeps current with professional literature and trends in recovery support. Attends continuing education trainings, workshops, seminars, or conferences in order to keep current with evidenced based standards of practice and maintain certification.
  • Maintains confidentiality of all materials handled within the Network/Entity as well as the proper release of information.
  • Complies with Network and departmental policies regarding issues of employee, patient and environmental safety and follows appropriate reporting requirements.
  • Demonstrates/models the Network’s Service Excellence Standards of Performance in interactions with all customers (internal and external).
  • Demonstrates financial responsibility and accountability through the effective and efficient use of resources in daily procedures, processes, and practices.
  • Complies with Network and departmental policies regarding attendance and dress code.
  • Other duties as assigned​

PHYSICAL AND SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:

Sitting for up to 5 hours per day, 2 hours at a time. Standing for up to 1 hour per day, 1 hour at a time. Walking for up to 2 hours per day, 20 minutes at a time. Occasionally uses fingers to turn pages. Frequently uses hands to write, type, and hold charts. Rarely uses the hands or fingers for firm grasping or twisting/turning. Frequently uses upper extremities to lift and carry up to 10 pounds. Frequently stoops, occasionally squats, rarely reaches above shoulder level. Hearing as it relates to normal conversation in person or on telephone. Seeing as it relates to general vision, near vision, far vision, color vision, and peripheral vision.

EDUCATION:

Must be a Certified Recovery Specialist (CRS) or Certified Family Recovery Specialist (CFRS) preferred, or eligible to earn the CRS or CFRS certification, or similar certification.

TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:

Understanding of principals of addiction and recovery.

Language, Mathematical Reasoning ability needed.

Additionally, you are encouraged to upload a current resume, including all work history, education, and/or certifications and licenses, if applicable. It is highly recommended that you create a profile at the conclusion of submitting your first application. Thank you for your interest in St. Luke's!!

title: Wealth Management Advisor
description:
As a wealth management advisor, you’re responsible for developing and maintaining lasting and trusting business relationships with members and clients, to ensure they’re satisfied. Your role is to listen to members’ and clients’ needs, offer them advice that fits their financial situation and help them choose appropriate solutions to meet their financial goals. You work closely with a client base consisting of individual members and business owners. Interpersonal savvy is therefore essential. You drive results by developing strategies and recommending investments, loans and insurance products. You use your expertise to balance member/client satisfaction, business objectives, profitability and sound and prudent risk management. You work with various partners and experts to design integrated strategies that meet the needs of members and clients. More specifically, you will be required to:

  • Advise members and clients on the best strategies and work with them to identify expected results.
  • Manage business relationships, assess member/client satisfaction and service quality, follow up and identify areas for improvement.
  • Stay up-to-date on the financial services industry, market trends and best practices in your field.
  • Participate in outreach activities and represent the caisse in the community.

What we offer*

  • Competitive salary and annual bonus
  • 4 weeks of flexible vacation starting in the first year
  • Defined benefit pension plan that provides predictable, stable income throughout retirement
  • Group insurance including telemedicine
  • Reimbursement of health and wellness expenses and telework equipment

* Benefits apply based on eligibility criteria.


What you bring to the table

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field
  • A minimum of one year of relevant experience
  • Please note that other combinations of qualifications and relevant experience may be considered
  • Mutual fund representative certificate – Autorité des marchés financiers
  • Knowledge of French is required
  • Knowledge of current financial, economic, political and legislative events
  • Specialized knowledge of tax, financial and succession issues for individuals and businesses
  • Knowledge of all products and services aimed at caisse members and those offered by Desjardins Business Centres, Desjardins components and distribution networks, and those offered by competitors
  • Knowledge of debt management
  • Knowledge of compliance with legislation respecting the distribution of financial products and services
  • Understanding of the philosophy and fundamentals of financial services cooperatives
  • Knowledge of policies, legislation and standards related to products and services offered by the caisse
  • Knowledge of the Desjardins business processes
Action oriented, Customer Focus, Differences, Drive results, Interpersonal Savvy, Nimble learning
